Through multiple experiments, we evaluated the impact of different deep learning backbones, data augmentation strategies, and generalizability, benchmarking our method against a recent state-of-the-art approach and validating it clinically against seven experienced clinicians. Results showed that the mean errors in caliper placement and biometric calculations for our model were comparable to those of human experts. Consequently, this framework offers a pathway for clinical translation, enabling novice users in resource-limited settings to perform reliable and standardized assessments of fetal brain sonograms.

We present natural connectivity as a robustness metric for complex networks, offering both a clear physical interpretation and a straightforward mathematical definition. This measure quantifies path redundancy by calculating the weighted count of closed walks across all lengths. Mathematically, natural connectivity emerges as an average eigenvalue from the graph spectrum and strictly increases monotonically as edges are added. Through a scenario of edge removal, we evaluate natural connectivity against other robustness metrics and demonstrate its sharp discriminatory power, which aligns with intuitive expectations.

Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, one-dimensional formal groups are categorized by their height. For $K3$ surfaces, this height is an integer ranging from $1$ to $10$ or infinity. In the case of Calabi-Yau threefolds, the height is finite and bounded by $h^{1,2}+1$, where $h^{1,2}$ denotes a Hodge number. Currently, explicit examples with known height values or their distribution are scarce. This paper examines Calabi-Yau threefolds derived from weighted Delsarte threefolds in positive characteristic. We present an algorithm to calculate the height of their formal groups and perform computations on various Delsarte-type Calabi-Yau threefolds.

An $n \times n \times p$ tensor is referred to as a T-square tensor, which appears frequently in applications like image feature extraction and multi-view clustering. A T-square tensor can be symmetrized into a T-symmetric tensor. For every T-square tensor, a T-quadratic form is defined, taking an $n \times p$ matrix as input and producing a $p$-dimensional vector as output. Additionally, eigentuples and eigenmatrices are established for T-square tensors. It is demonstrated that T-symmetric tensors possess unique largest and smallest eigentuples, and that a T-quadratic form is positive semi-definite (or definite) if and only if its smallest eigentuple is nonnegative (or positive). Furthermore, the connections between the eigen-decomposition of T-symmetric tensors and the TSVD of general third-order tensors are investigated.

Established in 2018, the Better Scientific Software Fellowship (BSSwF) aims to enhance developer productivity and the long-term sustainability of scientific software by fostering effective practices, processes, and tools. The fellowship's vision involves expanding the community through practitioners, leaders, mentors, and consultants, thereby raising the profile of scientific software production and sustainability. Over the past five years, numerous fellows and honorable mentions have embraced the role of research software engineer (RSE). This paper presents case studies of various program participants to demonstrate the diverse benefits BSSwF has provided to both RSEs and the broader scientific community. In an environment where RSE contributions are frequently undervalued, we posit that initiatives like BSSwF serve as a vital mechanism to recognize and motivate community members to transcend their routine obligations, thereby expanding their work, collaborations, and ideas to a wider audience.

This paper investigates Galois LCD codes, a more general framework for complementary dual codes, using a unified approach. We establish a necessary and sufficient condition for linear codes to qualify as Galois LCD codes and characterize those constacyclic codes that satisfy this property. Additionally, we provide illustrative examples of constacyclic codes that are simultaneously Galois LCD and MDS codes. Particular attention is given to Hermitian LCD constacyclic codes, and we conclude by presenting a construction method for a class of codes that are both Hermitian LCD and MDS.

This paper aims to prove global well-posedness for a wide range of strictly hyperbolic Cauchy problems featuring coefficients that are $C^2$ in time, smooth in space, grow polynomially with respect to $x$, and exhibit singularities at $t=0$. The analyzed problems are strictly hyperbolic relative to a general weight and a metric defined on the phase space. The singularity is characterized by the unbounded growth of the first and second time-derivatives of the coefficients, permitting logarithmic or oscillatory behavior as $t$ approaches zero. To derive an energy estimate, we apply a conjugation using a pseudodifferential operator, $e^{\nu(t)\Theta(x,D_x)}$. In this framework, $\Theta(x,D_x)$ quantifies the loss by connecting it to the phase space metric and the singular nature of the problem, while $\nu(t)$ establishes the scale of that loss. We designate this conjugating operator as the *loss operator*; based on its order, we demonstrate that the solution may suffer zero, arbitrarily small, finite, or infinite loss compared to the initial data. Furthermore, we present a counterexample and establish anisotropic cone conditions within this context.

Assuming the dark sector comprises a dark scalar $\phi$ and a dark fermion $\chi$ governed by an exact $Z_2$ symmetry, the sterile neutrino $N$ serves as a portal to the Standard Model through the Yukawa interaction $\lambda_{ds} \bar{\chi}\phi N$. This study specifically investigates the regime where $m_N > m_\phi + m_\chi$, identifying $\chi$ as a FIMP dark matter candidate. The decay rate of the dark scalar $\phi$ is significantly suppressed by both the small Yukawa coupling $\lambda_{ds}$ and the mixing angle $\theta$. Consequently, the delayed decay process $\phi \to \chi\nu$ profoundly influences cosmological metrics, including Big Bang Nucleosynthesis, Cosmic Microwave Background anisotropy, the effective number of relativistic neutrino species ($N_{\rm eff}$), and high-energy neutrino fluxes. Additionally, when $m_N < m_W$, the sterile neutrino can produce displaced vertex signatures at colliders, while the dark scalar $\phi$ may trigger observable Higgs invisible decays for sufficiently large quartic couplings. This paper presents a thorough analysis of constraints derived from both cosmological and collider data, concluding that nearly the entire parameter space with $m_N < m_W$ is accessible to future experimental probes.

For a locally compact group bundle, we demonstrate that the system of Plancherel weights associated with their C*-algebras exhibits lower semi-continuity. Consequently, this result implies that the dual Haar system corresponding to a continuous Haar system on a locally compact abelian group bundle remains continuous.

The Yoccoz inequality establishes an $O(1/q)$ limit on the dimensions of $p/q$-limbs within the Mandelbrot set. For more than three decades, it has been hypothesized that this limit could be refined to $O(1/q^2)$. By employing parabolic implosion, we present the initial instance of a limb family adhering to this enhanced bound, specifically the $1/q$-limbs, and further demonstrate that the $O(1/q^2)$ constraint is optimal for this particular set.

Several teams engage in a random competition where each round awards a single point to the winner. This study investigates the duration until ties occur between these teams, utilizing constructed martingales and supermartingales to establish findings regarding these stopping times. The research is driven by its relevance to database systems and their storage engines, which rely on augmented balanced search trees. Specifically, the occurrences of ties in the competition correspond to the required rebalancing operations within the database.

We present the initial construction of stationary measures for the open KPZ equation on the spatial interval $[0,1]$, subject to general inhomogeneous Neumann boundary conditions at $0$ and $1$ parameterized by real values $u$ and $v$, respectively. For the case where $u+v\geq 0$, we uniquely identify these stationary measures by their multipoint Laplace transform, which we demonstrate corresponds to a stochastic process termed the continuous dual Hahn process.

This paper presents a class of time-varying controllers for Euler-Lagrange systems that ensure convergence within an arbitrary finite time, regardless of initial conditions, and without inducing chattering. The proposed approach utilizes a mapping technique structured in two stages: initially, a standard asymptotically stable controller (specifically for obstacle avoidance) is defined for the nominal system; subsequently, a prescribed-time controller (also for obstacle avoidance) is derived for the perturbed system through a straightforward substitution. The study demonstrates that the proposed scheme achieves uniform prescribed-time stability for unperturbed systems and prescribed-time attractivity for perturbed systems, effectively rejecting matched disturbances with unknown upper bounds without requiring disturbance observation. Numerical simulations illustrate this approach using a two-link robot manipulator.

Next-generation CMB experiments aim to precisely constrain the tensor-to-scalar ratio, $r$. Since the observed CMB $B$-mode polarization signal from primordial tensor perturbations is overwhelmed by gravitational lensing, delensing is critical. To achieve this effectively, researchers must look beyond the traditional quadratic estimator (QE), which is becoming suboptimal, and the maximum a posteriori estimator, which is still in development. Caldeira et al. (2020) demonstrated that a neural network (NN) using the ResUNet architecture outperforms the QE but remains slightly suboptimal compared to an iterative estimator for lensing reconstruction. This study advances those findings by evaluating how these estimators perform in delensing maps containing primordial tensor perturbations using a standard pipeline. Results from simulations with $r=0.01$ and $r=0.001$, covering $12.7^{\circ} \times 12.7^{\circ}$ maps at CMB-Stage~4 noise levels ($1\,\mu \rm{K\,arcmin}$) and a 1' beam, show that the NN estimator achieves optimal delensing performance, matching the converged iterative estimator. Furthermore, we establish that for delensing, NNs must be trained and evaluated on CMB maps with multipoles $l<l_{\rm{cut}}$ removed to prevent spurious correlations in the final delensed $B$-mode power spectrum, a requirement consistent with previous findings for QEs and iterative methods. Finally, we outline various NN training strategies that can be adapted for simultaneously handling foregrounds and complex instrumental effects where modeling uncertainties are higher.

Kernel methods have long been a cornerstone of machine learning, relying on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) to solve various learning tasks. This paper introduces a new data analysis framework based on the reproducing kernel Hilbert $C^*$-module (RKHM) and kernel mean embedding (KME) defined within an RKHM. Because RKHM encompasses richer information than standard RKHS or vector-valued RKHS (vvRKHS), utilizing it allows for the effective capture and extraction of structural properties, such as those found in functional data. We develop a theoretical foundation for applying RKHM to data analysis, covering the representer theorem, as well as the injectivity and universality of our proposed KME. Furthermore, we demonstrate that RKHM generalizes both RKHS and vvRKHS. Finally, we outline specific procedures for implementing RKHM and the proposed KME in practical data analysis scenarios.

This paper addresses the challenge of determining the minimum and maximum probabilities of satisfying an $\omega$-regular property within a bounded-parameter Markov decision process (BMDP). BMDPs extend standard Markov decision processes (MDPs) by introducing uncertainty into transition probabilities, representing them as intervals where exact values are unknown. $\omega$-regular properties constitute a broad class of specifications, expressible through structures like Rabin or parity automata, and include complex requirements such as those in linear temporal logic. In a BMDP, the likelihood of satisfying such a property is contingent upon both the unknown transition probabilities and the chosen policy. Our approach calculates these extreme probability values, thereby resolving a specific problem posed by Dutreix and Coogan at CDC 2018. This work generalizes their findings on interval Markov chains (which lacked an adversary) by reinterpreting their analysis through the lens of interval MDPs and framing the BMDP problem as an analysis of an $\omega$-regular stochastic game. Furthermore, this methodology extends naturally to bounded-parameter stochastic games.

Non-local correlations in entangled systems are typically quantified using Bell's inequality violations. Recent research has demonstrated that in neutrino systems, the Non-Local Advantage of Quantum Coherence (NAQC) serves as a more robust indicator of non-local correlations than Bell's inequality. This study investigates the impact of non-standard interactions (NSI) on both measures within two-flavor neutrino oscillations across the DUNE, MINOS, T2K, KamLAND, JUNO, and Daya Bay experimental configurations. Our findings indicate that while Bell's inequality violations persist across the entire energy spectrum even with NSI, NAQC violations are confined to specific energy ranges, underscoring the more fundamental nature of NAQC. Furthermore, NSI can amplify the violation of both NAQC and the Bell's inequality parameter at higher energies, with the most significant enhancements occurring in the KamLAND experiment. However, the potential increase in the Bell's inequality parameter over standard model predictions reaches up to 11%, compared to a 7% increase for NAQC. Consequently, although NAQC acts as a stronger witness of nonclassicality, it exhibits reduced sensitivity to NSI effects relative to the Bell's inequality parameter.

This paper introduces a method for inverting experimental in-plane, co-polarized light scattering data (both p and s polarizations) to determine the normalized surface-height autocorrelation function and the root-mean-square (rms) roughness of two-dimensional randomly rough metal surfaces. The technique relies on an expression derived from second-order phase perturbation theory, which calculates the mean differential reflection coefficient's contribution from diffusely scattered light. The validity of this inversion scheme is confirmed using multiple sets of simulated scattering data for rough silver surfaces characterized by Gaussian height correlation functions. The reconstructions yield high accuracy for weakly rough surfaces under p- and s-polarized illumination, even when multiple scattering of surface plasmon polaritons contributes significantly to the input data. Furthermore, the method was applied to experimental scattering data from characterized two-dimensional randomly rough gold surfaces, producing results that align well with direct surface morphology analysis. These findings demonstrate the appeal of the proposed computationally efficient inversion scheme.

An irregular cusp in an orthogonal modular variety is defined as a point where the lattice governing the Fourier expansion is strictly contained within the lattice of translations. The existence of such cusps significantly impacts the investigation of pluricanonical forms on the variety through the lens of modular forms. This work examines the toroidal compactification relative to an irregular cusp and elucidates the cusp form criterion necessary for computing the Kodaira dimension in this context. Furthermore, we demonstrate that irregular cusps are relatively rare: aside from instances involving neat groups or those containing -1, we establish that the stable orthogonal groups associated with most (though not all) even lattices lack irregular cusps.

This paper aims to demonstrate the $L^p$-$L^q$ boundedness of H\"ormander's Fourier multipliers within the context of commutative hypergroups. To achieve this, we derive the Paley inequality and the Hausdorff-Young-Paley inequality for such hypergroups. By applying these findings to Ch\'{e}bli-Trim\`{e}che hypergroups, we establish the $L^p$-$L^q$ boundedness of spectral multipliers associated with the generalised radial Laplacian. Consequently, we derive embedding theorems and time asymptotics regarding the $L^p$-$L^q$ norms of the heat kernel for this Laplacian. Finally, we illustrate how these results apply to analyzing the well-posedness of nonlinear partial differential equations.

Gerrymandering stands as a primary concern in modern American society, with the drafting of new voting maps and their ensuing legal battles dominating contemporary political dialogue. The ongoing legal, societal, and political debate regarding viable voting districts requires a notion of fairness—a vaguely defined and ill-specified concept that has resisted precise articulation. We propose a novel framework for comparing voting maps that circumvents the drawbacks of applying a single, pre-established metric uniformly. Instead, our evaluation approach utilizes uncertain data envelopment analysis to assess maps across multiple dimensions, allowing each district to be evaluated individually and optimally. We demonstrate this methodology by applying it to a set of proposed and publicly accessible maps to illustrate our assessment strategy.

A pivotal technology for next-generation cellular networks involves full duplex (FD) integrated access and backhaul (IAB) systems operating within millimeter-wave (mmWave) bands. The primary obstacle in deploying FD-IAB networks is effectively managing self-interference (SI) across these wideband mmWave frequencies. This study begins by outlining 3GPP IAB architectures and wideband mmWave channel models. By implementing a subarray-based hybrid precoding approach at FD-IAB nodes, multiuser interference is suppressed via zero-forcing at the transmitter, while remaining SI—after applying antenna and analog cancellation techniques—is eliminated using a minimum mean square error (MMSE) baseband combiner at the receiver. Spectral efficiency (SE) is assessed considering RF insertion loss (RFIL) alongside various phase shifter types and channel uncertainties. Simulation outcomes indicate that, despite RFIL, spectral efficiency nearly doubles compared to half-duplex systems when approaching the performance of fully connected hybrid precoding, provided that channel uncertainties remain minimal.

This study develops a stability theory for inhomogeneous fluids exposed to standing acoustic waves. Beginning with first principles, we derive a stability criterion for two immiscible fluids with distinct acoustic impedances separated by a planar interface. Combining theoretical analysis with numerical simulations, we demonstrate that interfacial tension governs the movement of the high-impedance fluid from anti-nodes to nodes once the acoustic force surpasses the tension force, a finding consistent with recent microchannel experiments. Additionally, we introduce an acoustic Bond number to distinguish between stable ($Bo_a < 1$) and relocation ($Bo_a > 1$) regimes. Notably, we observe that increasing the channel height substantially lowers the critical acoustic energy density needed for fluid relocation, offering a valuable design strategy for acoustofluidic devices managing immiscible fluids.

This study details our methodology for training a neural network to identify hate speech in Hindi and Bengali. We also investigate the application of transfer learning to these languages, leveraging their shared origins and inherent similarities. Despite being executed with limited computational resources, our results are comparable to those achieved by more resource-intensive models. Moreover, given the relatively small training dataset and the fact that both languages are largely unfamiliar to us, this work serves as a generalized effort to demystify lost or alien languages that may be beyond human comprehension.

Although it is widely recognized that different algorithms often perform better on different subsets of computational problems, researchers predominantly focus on identifying a single optimal configuration based on aggregate metrics like averages. This paper introduces Integer Programming-based methods for constructing decision trees to address the Algorithm Selection Problem. These techniques automate three critical tasks: (i) identifying the most significant problem features to define problem classes; (ii) clustering problems into these classes; and (iii) selecting the best algorithm configuration for each class. To assess this new approach, extensive experiments were conducted using linear programming algorithms within the COIN-OR Branch & Cut solver across a broad range of instances, including all MIPLIB benchmarks. The outcomes surpassed our expectations. While choosing the single best parameter setting across all instances reduced total runtime by 22%, our method achieved an average runtime reduction of 40% over 10-fold cross-validation experiments. These findings suggest that our method generalizes effectively without overfitting.

Over time, researchers have extensively investigated numerous graph problems, particularly those classified as NP-complete, with notable instances including graph coloring, the traveling salesman problem, and subgraph isomorphism. Traditionally, these challenges are tackled using exact algorithms, approximation methods, and heuristics, yet each approach carries inherent limitations. Recently, the application of learning-based frameworks, such as machine learning techniques, has gained traction for solving these issues, leveraging their ability to identify novel patterns within graph-structured data. This emerging field has garnered significant interest. The present survey offers a systematic examination of classic graph problems where learning-based solutions have been proposed. We analyze the design and performance of various frameworks and highlight potential avenues for future research. Ultimately, this work aims to provide clearer insights and serve as a foundational resource for the research community advancing in this domain.

Integrating range sensors with color cameras offers significant advantages for robotic tasks such as navigation, semantic understanding, manipulation, and telepresence. While various methods for fusing color and depth data have been developed and applied successfully, most systems struggle with noise in range data and resolution mismatches, as current range sensors typically offer lower resolution than color cameras. Although stereo matching can generate high-resolution depth maps, it often fails in scenes with weak or repetitive textures or complex self-occlusions. In contrast, range sensors provide coarse depth information independent of texture. A calibrated system combining a time-of-flight (TOF) camera with a stereoscopic pair can overcome the limitations of individual sensors through data fusion. We introduce a novel TOF-stereo fusion method utilizing an efficient seed-growing algorithm, where TOF data projected onto the stereo images serve as initial correspondences. These "seeds" are propagated using a Bayesian model that integrates image similarity scores with rough depth priors derived from low-resolution range data. This approach yields dense, accurate depth maps at the resolution of the available color cameras. Our results demonstrate that this algorithm surpasses 2D image-based stereo methods and achieves higher resolution than commercial color-range sensors like the Kinect, while potentially delivering real-time performance on a single CPU.

An investigation into singly produced vector-like quarks, specifically the $T$ quark ($+2/3$ charge) and the $Y$ quark ($-4/3$ charge), was conducted using proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. This dataset, with an integrated luminosity of $36.1 \text{fb}^{-1}$, was collected by the ATLAS detector at the LHC during 2015 and 2016. The study focused on $Q \to Wb$ decay channels where the $W$ boson undergoes a leptonic decay. Results showed no significant deviation from the predicted Standard Model background. Consequently, upper limits were established for the $QWb$ coupling strength and the mixing between the Standard Model and either a singlet $T$ or $Y$ quark arising from a $(B,Y)$ doublet or $(T,B,Y)$ triplet, accounting for interference with Standard Model processes. The derived upper bounds on the mixing angles are $|\sin{\theta_{\text{L}}}|= 0.18$ for an 800 GeV singlet $T$ quark, $|\sin{\theta_{\text{R}}}|= 0.17$ for an 800 GeV $Y$ quark in a $(B,Y)$ doublet, and $|\sin{\theta_{\text{L}}}|= 0.16$ for an 800 GeV $Y$ quark in a $(T,B,Y)$ triplet. Notably, within the $(B,Y)$ doublet framework, the constraints on the mixing parameter $|\sin{\theta_{\text{R}}}|$ align with those from electroweak precision observables for masses ranging approximately from 900 GeV to 1250 GeV.

A Hawkes process defined on $\mathbb{R}$ is a point process where the intensity at time $t$ depends functionally on its historical activity prior to $t$, determined by an activation function $\Phi$ and a memory function $h$. This study characterizes the Hawkes property as an operator acting on the subspace of non-negative sequences representing inter-point distances. Leveraging the standard relationship between stationary point processes and their Palm measures, the authors demonstrate that the corresponding Palm measure can be described as an invariant distribution of a Markovian kernel. It is proven that a stationary Hawkes point process exists provided $\Phi$ is continuous, exhibits at most linear growth with a rate below a specific constant, thereby relaxing the classical Lipschitz condition required for unbounded $\Phi$ in existing literature. The methodology combines coupling techniques, monotonicity properties of linear Hawkes processes, and established results regarding Palm distributions. Additionally, analyzing the process initiated from the null measure on $\mathbb{R}_-$ (the empty state) is crucial, which also facilitates a re-examination of the linear Hawkes-Oakes case. Specifically, when the memory function $h$ is exponential, a stationary Hawkes process is shown to exist under weak conditions, with its Palm measure expressed via the invariant distribution of a one-dimensional Harris ergodic Markov chain. Conversely, if the activation function $\Phi$ is a polynomial of degree greater than one, a stationary Hawkes process cannot exist; however, in such scenarios starting from the empty state, a scaling result regarding the accumulation of points is derived.

This study examines a UAV-aided relay communication system designed to deliver ultra-reliable, low-latency messages, with the relay functioning in amplifier-and-forward (AF) mode. The primary objective is to jointly optimize the UAV's position and transmit power to reduce decoding error probability while satisfying latency requirements. The analysis incorporates both free-space and three-dimensional (3-D) channel models. For the free-space model, a low-complexity iterative algorithm is introduced, alongside a derivation of the globally optimal solution under extremely high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Similarly, a low-complexity iterative algorithm is proposed for the 3-D model. Simulation results validate the superior performance of the proposed algorithms.

This study assesses specific Catalan-Hankel Pfaffians using skew orthogonal polynomial theory. Leveraging the various hypergeometric orthogonal polynomials within the Askey scheme, we explicitly derive classical skew orthogonal polynomials and subsequently present diverse examples of Catalan-Hankel Pfaffians based on both continuous and $q$-moment sequences.

The advancement of large language models across numerous NLP tasks has driven researchers to utilize increasingly massive text corpora, many of which are scraped from the internet with scant documentation. This study offers some of the initial documentation for the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4), a dataset derived from filtering a single snapshot of Common Crawl. First, we trace the data's origins, revealing substantial content from unexpected sources such as patents and U.S. military websites. Next, we analyze the text's composition, identifying machine-generated material, including machine-translated content, as well as evaluation samples from other NLP benchmarks. To assess the impact of the filtering process, we examine the excluded text, demonstrating that blocklist filtering disproportionately removes content regarding and about minority individuals. Finally, we conclude with recommendations for creating and documenting web-scale datasets derived from internet scrapes.

While large Transformer-based language models assist human writers by proposing likely text continuations, existing interactive tools lack the capability to steer generation toward specific topics. To overcome this, we propose a framework that presents users with multiple candidate topics, allowing them to select a subset to guide the output. This system comprises two parts: first, a method that identifies candidate topics by predicting the centroids of word clusters within potential continuations, and second, a generation model constrained to adhere to the selected topics. Both components are trained in a self-supervised manner using only unlabeled text. Experimental results show that our proposed topics outperform standard clustering methods, and the framework frequently produces fluent sentences aligned with the chosen directions, as confirmed by automated metrics and human evaluation.

Although unconditional GANs like StyleGAN can produce high-quality, diverse, and photorealistic images, they offer limited control over the generation process using semantic attributes without compromising output quality. Additionally, the entangled nature of GAN latent spaces means that editing one attribute often causes unintended changes to others. This paper addresses conditional exploration within these entangled spaces by examining attribute-conditioned sampling and attribute-controlled editing as two key sub-problems. We introduce StyleFlow, a simple, effective, and robust solution that tackles both issues by framing conditional exploration as a conditional continuous normalizing flow within the GAN latent space, conditioned on attribute features. Our method is evaluated using the face and car latent spaces of StyleGAN, demonstrating fine-grained, disentangled edits across various attributes on both real photographs and synthetic images. For instance, in the context of faces, we successfully manipulate camera pose, lighting, expression, facial hair, gender, and age. Finally, extensive qualitative and quantitative comparisons confirm that StyleFlow outperforms other contemporary approaches.

The formation of Jovian planets is strongly linked to the metallicity of their host stars, which serves as an indicator for the abundance of solids in the protoplanetary disk. Prior observational studies suggest that these planets form more readily around stars with solar or super-solar metallicities. Consequently, forming planets in metal-poor environments remains difficult, especially for hot Jupiters believed to originate through metallicity-dependent core accretion. While previous searches for hot Jupiters around metal-poor stars exist, their small sample sizes—stemming from a scarcity of high-quality data—have made it challenging to constrain hot Jupiter occurrence in this regime until now. This study utilizes a large sample of halo stars observed by TESS to establish an upper limit on hot Jupiter occurrence within the metal-poor range (-2.0 $\leq$ [Fe/H] $\leq$ -0.6). By setting the most stringent upper limit, we determine the mean 1-$\sigma$ upper limit to be 0.18% for planets with radii between 0.8 and 2 R$_{\rm{Jupiter}}$ and periods ranging from 0.5 to 10 days. This finding aligns with prior predictions suggesting a specific metallicity threshold below which planet formation does not occur.

This paper examines various puzzles concerning the Rule of Existential Generalization (EG). From the perspective of simple type theory, I differentiate (EG) from a modified Rule of Existential Quantifier Introduction that can be derived from it. Although these two rules are frequently conflated and often treated as primitive, I demonstrate that (EG) is actually derivable from the proper Rule of Existential Quantifier Introduction. Furthermore, in logical frameworks accommodating both total and partial functions, this latter rule must be primitive because universal and existential quantifiers cannot be interdefined within such systems. An appropriate natural deduction system for this framework is presented, which is simpler than one recently proposed and applied by the author. This system employs a robust definition of substitution capable of addressing not only higher-order quantification but also (hyper)intensional contexts.

We introduce a technique for encoding path information from graphs into a 3-dimensional tensor and demonstrate its relationship with powered adjacency matrices. To address the high computational costs associated with this 3-D tensor, we propose applying dimensionality reduction along the depth axis. Subsequently, we show that this reduced 3-D matrix can be integrated into an established graph convolutional network framework, such as MixHop, to function as a viable graph convolutional layer.

Databases have been the subject of categorical research for many years. Typically, the database schema—which organizes high-level conceptual entities—is represented as a category or sketch, while the data itself, or instance, is modeled as a set-valued functor that maps each conceptual entity to a set of examples. Although these categorical frameworks are mathematically elegant, they have often struggled to represent concrete data types like integers or strings.

In this work, we propose an extension of the set-valued functor model that utilizes multisorted algebraic theories (also known as Lawvere theories) to integrate concrete data in a principled manner. This approach enables constraints and queries to operate on data using specific operations, such as number comparison or multiplication, thereby bridging the divide between traditional databases and programming languages.

Furthermore, we demonstrate that all components of our proposed model—including schemas, instances, change-of-schema functors, and queries—cohere within a unified double categorical structure known as a proarrow equipment (or framed bicategory).

Inspired by the needs of quantum networks operating over classical channels, we begin investigating $n$-party resource states that enable LOCC protocols to generate EPR pairs between any $k$ disjoint pairs of parties. We present constructions of these states where $k$ remains close to the theoretical maximum of $n/2$, requiring each party to maintain only a constant number of qubits. Specifically, in the scenario where each party holds a single qubit, we introduce a family of $n$-qubit states derived from Reed-Muller codes that achieves $k$ proportional to $\log n$, alongside numerically identified examples for $k=2$ and $k=3$. Furthermore, we establish lower bounds, demonstrating that achieving $k=n/2$ necessitates each party possessing at least $\Omega(\log\log n)$ qubits.

This study performs a longitudinal examination of the U.S. labor market's structure across seven decades of technological, economic, and policy shifts. By integrating network science, natural language processing, and machine learning, we identify structural transformations within the labor market over time. Our findings reveal a consistent rate of job disappearance alongside a gradual shift in required work tasks, despite the significant changes occurring during this period. Utilizing machine learning, we categorize occupations as primarily cognitive or physical based on textual descriptions of workplace duties. Furthermore, we observe a growing polarization between these two job categories, driven by the increasing similarity of tasks within them, which may hinder workers' ability to transition between different roles.

In magnetic field calculations, cylindrical permanent magnets are frequently modeled as ideal, azimuthally symmetric solenoids. Although this approximation is widely used, literature detailing its validity and constraints remains scarce. This study compares the analytically derived field of an ideal solenoid with the experimentally measured field of a cylindrical permanent magnet. We present an experimental setup designed to capture the magnetic field distribution, which enables the measurement of both axial and radial field components surrounding the magnet. The results show strong agreement between the experimental data and theoretical predictions, thereby confirming the reliability of the ideal solenoid model for forecasting the magnetic field distribution of permanent magnets.

Sample surveys have long served as a cost-effective means of estimating population and sub-population characteristics, a field known as "small area estimation." However, outliers in the data can severely distort these estimates, particularly in domains with limited sample sizes. Building on established robust estimators, we introduce two novel bias calibration approaches. Simulation results demonstrate that our methods yield more efficient estimates than other existing bias-calibration techniques. We further apply these estimators to calculate Gini coefficients for labor market areas in Tuscany, Italy, utilizing data from the EU-SILC survey and the Italian census; this application reveals insights distinct from those provided by current methods. Finally, we extend these concepts to generate predictions for non-sampled areas.

We introduce an online multi-view depth prediction method for posed video streams, efficiently and geometrically soundly propagating scene geometry calculated in prior frames to the current one. The core of our solution is a lightweight, real-time encoder-decoder architecture that utilizes cost volumes derived from image pairs. We enhance this framework by integrating a ConvLSTM cell at the bottleneck layer, enabling the compression of extensive historical data within its states. Our key innovation involves propagating the cell's hidden state by explicitly accounting for viewpoint shifts between time steps; specifically, we warp the previous hidden state into the current camera plane using the prior depth prediction. This extension incurs minimal computational and memory overhead while substantially improving depth estimation accuracy. Consequently, our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art multi-view stereo techniques on the majority of metrics across hundreds of indoor scenes, all while sustaining real-time performance. Code available: https://github.com/ardaduz/deep-video-mvs

The ACII Affective Vocal Bursts (A-VB) competition pioneers a new area within affective computing focused on recognizing human emotions through non-verbal sounds. While emotion detection via speech or facial expressions is well-established, non-verbal vocalizations like laughs, cries, and sighs remain underutilized despite their significant value in behavioral analysis. This challenge features four tasks designed to investigate non-verbal cues across various domains. This technical report details the methodology and outcomes of the SclabCNU Team for these tasks, demonstrating results that surpass the baseline model provided by the organizers.

This paper introduces 2-category theory through the lens of Gray-categories, employing the graphical calculus of separated surface diagrams. We illustrate this approach with an extended example involving cones and limits of 2-functors. Furthermore, by leveraging the canonical adjunction between 2-computads and 2-categories, we interpret the comparison structure of lax functors and expand the surface diagram calculus to include compositor sheets, enabling the representation and reasoning about these structures.

The recent identification of a new class of ultra-high-energy gamma-ray sources, with spectra reaching beyond 100 TeV, confirms the existence of Galactic PeVatrons—cosmic-ray accelerators capable of boosting particles to PeV energies. Aside from the Crab Nebula, these sources remain unidentified. Most span over one degree and host multiple potential counterparts, such as Supernova Remnants, young stellar clusters, and Pulsar Wind Nebulae (PWNe), which could serve as PeVatrons powering the surrounding diffuse ultra-high-energy gamma-ray structures. In PWNe, gamma rays are generated by electrons accelerated at the pulsar wind termination shock via inverse Compton scattering of 2.7 K CMB radiation. The high efficiency of converting pulsar rotational energy into relativistic electrons, along with short cooling times, enables gamma-ray luminosities up to $L_\gamma \sim 0.1 \dot{E}$. Furthermore, the pulsar spin-down luminosity, $\dot{E}$, sets the absolute maximum photon energy: $E_{\rm \gamma~\rm max}\approx 0.9 \dot{E}_{36}^{0.65}~~\rm{PeV}$. This constraint outweighs limits imposed by synchrotron losses for young PWNe with typical magnetic fields of $\approx$100$\mu$G and $\dot{E} \lesssim 10^{37}\ \rm erg/s$. We examine the implications of $E_{\rm \gamma~\rm max}$ by comparing it with the highest-energy photons detected by LHAASO from over a dozen ultra-high-energy sources. Whenever a PWN origin is plausible, we utilize LHAASO data to establish upper limits on the nebular magnetic field.

High entropy alloys (HEAs) have recently become a promising platform for identifying superconducting materials and investigating exotic superconducting phenomena. Given their highly disordered atomic structure, conventional phonon-mediated BCS superconductivity is considered unlikely, making the study of their microscopic properties essential. This work presents the first comprehensive analysis of the superconducting characteristics of two noncentrosymmetric HEAs with an $\alpha$-Mn structure—specifically {(HfNb)}$_{0.10}${(MoReRu)}$_{0.90}$ and {(ZrNb)}$_{0.10}${(MoReRu)}$_{0.90}$—through magnetization, specific heat, AC transport, and muon-spin relaxation/rotation ($\mu$SR) measurements. Despite their inherent disorder, low-temperature specific heat and transverse-field $\mu$SR data indicate a nodeless, isotropic superconducting gap, while zero-field $\mu$SR results confirm that time-reversal symmetry remains intact in the superconducting ground state.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable performance improvements for graph-structured tasks, particularly in natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Motivated by the success of transformer architectures, a growing number of studies have explored attention-based GNN variants to push the boundaries of these domains. Integrating "attention" mechanisms into graph mining is seen as a strategy to address the noise, heterogeneity, and complexity inherent in graph data, as well as to encode soft inductive biases. Consequently, it is essential and beneficial to examine these variants from a high-level perspective to evaluate their respective strengths and limitations. This work offers a systematic and focused tutorial on attention-based GNNs, aiming to assist researchers tackling graph-structured problems. The tutorial analyzes GNN variants through the lens of the attention function, progressively deepening the reader's comprehension of various graph attention mechanisms.

Conditional lower bounds derived from assumptions like $P\neq NP$ or the Exponential-Time Hypothesis (ETH) offer valuable insights into the potential capabilities of algorithms. Ideally, these bounds prove that existing algorithms are fundamentally optimal and cannot be significantly improved. This tutorial surveys various types of lower bounds and explores their application to database theory and constraint satisfaction problems.

The task of learning to search involves developing artificial agents capable of autonomously utilizing search interfaces to locate information. While existing language models have demonstrated the ability to learn symbolic query reformulation strategies when paired with traditional term-based retrieval, they have yet to surpass the performance of neural retrievers. This study expands the learning-to-search framework into a hybrid environment that supports discrete query refinement operations following an initial retrieval phase executed by a dual encoder. Evaluations on the BEIR benchmark reveal that search agents trained through behavioral cloning exceed the performance of the underlying system, which combines a dual encoder retriever with a cross-encoder reranker. Additionally, we observe that straightforward heuristic Hybrid Retrieval Environments (HRE) can boost baseline performance by several nDCG points. The HRE-based search agent (HARE) achieves state-of-the-art results in both zero-shot and in-domain assessments. Finally, we conduct a comprehensive qualitative analysis to illuminate the policies governing these agents.

Identifying small, low-conductivity inclusions within a uniform medium using low-frequency electrical field data is crucial for medical electrical impedance tomography and geological electrical resistivity tomography. These objects can be described by a Pólya-Szegő (polarizability) tensor, a characterization that has gained attention because it supplies object features for machine learning classifiers and offers an alternative imaging approach. However, training machine learning models necessitates large dictionaries and demands high accuracy in these characterizations. This study derives precise numerical approximations of the tensor coefficients using an adaptive boundary element method. The objective is to generate a series of benchmark computations for these coefficients, enabling other software developers to verify the accuracy of their implementations.

The Belle Collaboration has recently reported the $\Xi(1620)$ state, previously listed in the Particle Data Group (PDG) with a single star, in the $\Xi^{-}\pi^{+}$ channel. Its properties, including spectroscopy and decay width, defy simple explanation within conventional constituent quark models, sparking active debate regarding its structure. In this study, we investigate the radiative decays of this newly observed $\Xi(1620)$ under the assumption that it is a $\Lambda\bar{K}$-$\Sigma\bar{K}$ meson-baryon molecular state with spin-parity $J^P=1/2^{-}$, as proposed in our prior work. Using effective Lagrangians, we calculate the partial decay widths for transitions into $\Xi\gamma$ and $\Xi\pi\gamma$ final states via hadronic loops. The estimated partial widths for $\Xi(1620)^0\to\gamma\Xi$ and $\Xi(1620)^0\to\gamma\Xi\pi$ are approximately $118.76\text{--}174.21$ keV and $58.19\text{--}68.75$ eV, respectively, making them potentially observable at LHCb. If the $\Xi(1620)$ is indeed a $\Lambda\bar{K}$-$\Sigma\bar{K}$ molecule, the radiative transition strength for $\Xi(1620)^0\to\gamma\bar{K}\Lambda$ is extremely weak, with a decay width on the order of 0.01 eV. Future experimental measurements of these channels will be valuable for testing the molecular interpretation of the $\Xi(1620)$.

This study derives all eighteen Gauss hypergeometric representations for the Ferrers function of the second kind, each featuring a distinct argument. These are generated from the eighteen hypergeometric forms of the associated Legendre function of the second kind via a limit representation. For each of the eighteen resulting arguments, we provide geometric descriptions of their convergence regions within the complex plane. Additionally, a corresponding single-sum Fourier expansion for the Ferrers function of the second kind is examined. In four of the eighteen instances, determining the Ferrers function requires evaluating the hypergeometric function separately above and below the branch cut on $[1,\infty)$. To finalize these derivations, we apply established results to formulate expressions for the hypergeometric function on both sides of its branch cut. Finally, we offer a comprehensive review of Richard Olbricht's 1888 paper, which was the first to investigate hypergeometric representations of Legendre functions.

Optimizing combinatorial structures is fundamental to numerous real-world challenges, particularly in the life sciences. A critical step in antibody design, for instance, involves identifying amino acid arrangements within a protein sequence that enhance pathogen binding. This combinatorial optimization is challenging due to vast search spaces and non-linear objectives; even for relatively small antibody design tasks with an eleven-amino-acid sequence, one must evaluate approximately 2.05 x 10^14 potential structures. Traditional Reinforcement Learning methods like Q-learning often yield poor results in such combinatorial contexts. We introduce Structured Q-learning (SQL), an extension of Q-learning that integrates structural priors specifically for combinatorial optimization. Leveraging a molecular docking simulator, we show that SQL successfully identifies high-binding-energy sequences and outperforms baseline methods across eight demanding antibody design tasks, including the development of antibodies for SARS-COV.

Drawing inspiration from natural example classes, we introduce generalized directed semi-trees and establish weighted shifts upon them. For an $n$-tuple of directed semi-trees satisfying specific criteria, we link it to an $n$-tuple of multiplication operators acting on the Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}^2(\beta)$ of formal power series. Under particular conditions, $\mathscr{H}^2(\beta)$ becomes a reproducing kernel Hilbert space containing holomorphic functions on a domain within $\mathbb C^n$, rendering the $n$-tuple of multiplication operators unitarily equivalent to an $n$-tuple of weighted shifts on these generalized directed semi-trees. Lastly, we present two distinct classes of operator $n$-tuples that can be inherently recognized as weighted shifts on generalized directed semi-trees.

This research introduces nonparametric analysis of deviance tools for generalized partially linear models utilizing local polynomial fitting. Under the assumption of a canonical link, we derive formulas for both local and global deviance that exhibit an additivity property, simplifying to analysis of variance decompositions when the data follows a Gaussian distribution. To formally assess the significance of the nonparametric component, we propose chi-square tests derived from integrated likelihood functions. Simulation studies demonstrate the performance of these tests and compare them against an existing penalized splines approach. Finally, the proposed methodology is applied to data from the German Bundesbank and the Federal Reserve.

Camera pose regression techniques estimate the camera's pose through a single forward pass on the input image, providing a swift and lightweight alternative to traditional image-retrieval-based localization. These methods jointly learn two regression tasks, utilizing a single embedding vector derived from a convolutional backbone to simultaneously determine camera position and orientation. We introduce an attention-based pose regression framework that treats convolutional activation maps as sequential inputs. By employing Transformers to encode these sequential maps into latent vectors for pose regression, our approach enables the model to attend to spatially varying deep features. Furthermore, we utilize two distinct Transformer heads to independently focus on features most informative for estimating position versus orientation. Our proposed method outperforms contemporary pose regressors, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on various outdoor and indoor benchmarks. Notably, to our knowledge, it is the sole method to achieve sub-meter average accuracy in outdoor scenes. We have made our code publicly available.

Crystal structure prediction remains one of the most significant unsolved challenges in materials science. Traditionally, this task is framed as a global optimization problem, where global search algorithms are paired with first-principles free energy calculations to determine the ground-state crystal structure based solely on chemical composition. However, these conventional *ab initio* methods often fail to leverage extensive implicit physicochemical rules and geometric constraints (deep knowledge) inherent in the vast repository of known crystal structures. Drawing inspiration from the deep learning revolution in protein structure prediction, we introduce AlphaCrystal, a novel algorithm that integrates a deep residual neural network to learn deep knowledge for predicting atomic contact maps, followed by 3D structure reconstruction via genetic algorithms. Experimental results on a benchmark set of crystal materials demonstrate that AlphaCrystal can generate structures closely matching the ground truth. Furthermore, by predicting and utilizing the contact map, the method accelerates the prediction process and holds the potential to manage larger systems. We believe this deep learning-based *ab initio* approach, which learns from existing material data, can scale up current crystal structure prediction practices. To our knowledge, AlphaCrystal represents the first neural network-based algorithm for predicting crystal structure contact maps and the first method capable of directly reconstructing crystal structures from material composition, with potential for further optimization through DFT calculations.

We examine mid-infrared (IR) emission within the Orion Bar photodissociation region by utilizing archival photometric and spectroscopic data from UKIRT, Spitzer, ISO, and SOFIA. Our analysis covers flux densities at specific emission bands (3.3, 3.4, 3.6, 6.6, 7.7, and 11.2 $\mu$m) across multiple sites, alongside a continuous spectrum from 3 to 45 $\mu$m in a single location. We analyze variations in band flux ratios, which respond to external conditions, by correlating them with distance from an ionizing source. Based on the assumption that mid-IR emission primarily originates from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs)—with a weak 3.4 $\mu$m feature linked to hydrogenated PAHs (H-PAHs)—we employ a PAH evolution model to track how populations of PAHs with varying sizes, hydrogenation levels, and ionization states change across the Orion Bar over a timescale comparable to its lifetime. Using these derived PAH ensembles, we generate synthetic spectra and band flux densities. The model successfully reproduces key features of the ratios $I_{3.6}/I_{11.2}$, $I_{7.7}/I_{11.2}$, $I_{7.7}/I_{3.6}$, and $I_{3.3}/I_{3.4}$. Our results indicate that the optimal match between observations and modeling occurs when carbon loss in PAHs is constrained by a carbon count of $N_{\rm C}=60$, supporting the attribution of the 3.4 $\mu$m band to H-PAHs. Furthermore, we confirm that large cations prevail at the PDR surface, whereas small neutral PAHs and anions are more abundant deeper within the molecular cloud.

This paper introduces a spatial active noise control (ANC) technique that utilizes individual kernel interpolation for both primary and secondary sound fields. Unlike traditional spatial ANC, which employs multiple secondary sources and microphones to eliminate unwanted noise across a continuous area, this approach leverages kernel interpolation to achieve flexible noise attenuation over target regions regardless of array geometry. Additionally, by incorporating a directional weighting kernel, the method accounts for prior knowledge regarding the direction of primary noise sources. Previous approaches, however, applied directional weights to the combined sound field rather than isolating the primary component, which constrained performance gains. The proposed solution addresses this by separately interpolating the primary and secondary fields and developing a corresponding normalized least-mean-square algorithm. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that this individual interpolation strategy yields superior performance compared to methods relying on total kernel interpolation.

High-quality models depend on high-quality training data. However, for overparameterized deep learning systems, the causal link between training data and model outputs remains increasingly unclear and poorly understood. Influence analysis helps clarify these underlying interactions by measuring how much each training example affects the final model. While calculating exact influence is provably difficult in the worst-case scenario, this challenge has spurred the creation of influence estimators that approximate true influence values. This paper presents the first comprehensive survey of training data influence analysis and estimation. We start by formalizing various, sometimes orthogonal, definitions of training data influence. Next, we categorize state-of-the-art influence analysis methods into a taxonomy, detailing each approach and comparing their assumptions, asymptotic complexities, and respective strengths and weaknesses. Finally, we suggest future research directions to enhance the practical utility, theoretical rigor, and empirical soundness of influence analysis. A curated, up-to-date list of related resources is available at https://github.com/ZaydH/influence_analysis_papers.

Recent breakthroughs in deep learning have significantly enhanced the capabilities of deepfake generation, producing increasingly realistic synthetic media. While these technologies hold promise for diverse applications and have garnered substantial interest from both academic and industrial sectors, they also raise profound social and criminal issues. This chapter examines the progression and inherent challenges of creating and detecting deepfakes. It further explores strategies to bolster the robustness of detection systems across various media types, including in-the-wild images and videos. Finally, the text outlines recommended directions for future research in the field of synthetic media.

Achieving decarbonized energy systems demands the scaling of renewable and flexible technologies within power sectors. This study compares six capacity expansion models to determine the optimal deployment of base-load and peak-load plants, electricity storage, and transmission infrastructure. We analyze four simplified, harmonized scenarios that isolate the impact of expanding single or paired technologies. Our findings reveal that variations in assumed availability factors cause significant technology-specific discrepancies in optimal capacity across nearly all scenarios. Furthermore, fixed energy-to-power ratios for storage can fundamentally alter expansion outcomes, particularly by shifting the balance between short- and long-duration storage, while fixed initial and terminal storage levels influence the seasonal utilization of long-duration assets. Models utilizing a pre-ordered dispatch structure diverge markedly from linear optimization approaches, as limited foresight and flexibility often necessitate higher capacity investments. Additionally, a simplified net transfer capacity method underestimates grid infrastructure requirements compared to a detailed direct current load flow approach. We also observe regional variations in optimal storage and transmission expansion, attributing these differences to distinct variable renewable generation and demand profiles. Although these general effects were identified in our stylized framework, we anticipate they remain relevant in more detailed modeling applications, albeit potentially with reduced visibility.

This paper presents Multi-Narrative Semantic Overlap (MNSO), a significant but under-researched NLP task focused on generating semantic overlaps across multiple alternative narratives. Due to the lack of an existing benchmark, we constructed a dataset by extracting 2,925 narrative pairs from the web and manually curating 411 ground-truth overlaps through human annotation. To evaluate this new task, we initially adapted the ROUGE metric from text summarization but found it inadequate. Consequently, we performed additional human validation to establish 200 document-level and 1,518 sentence-level ground-truth labels, which enabled the development of a novel precision-recall metric named SEM-F1 (semantic F1). Experimental results demonstrate that SEM-F1 exhibits a stronger correlation with human judgment and higher inter-rater agreement compared to ROUGE.

Motion in-betweening (MIB) involves creating intermediate skeletal movements between specified start and end poses while maintaining natural dynamics, such as the rhythmic stepping seen during walking. Although current state-of-the-art MIB techniques can produce reasonable motions from sparse key poses, they frequently lack the controllability needed to generate movements that align with specific semantic contexts required in real-world applications. This work focuses on a unified approach capable of handling both pose-conditioned and semantic-conditioned MIB tasks. Additionally, we introduce a motion augmentation strategy that enhances the quality of pose-conditioned generation by defining a distribution over smooth trajectories. Our proposed method surpasses existing state-of-the-art approaches in terms of pose prediction accuracy while offering greater controllability.

The generalized eigenvalue problem offers an efficient approach to determining extremal eigenvalues and eigenvectors within large quantum systems. By employing subspace projection, it constructs Hamiltonian and norm matrices based on a collection of non-orthogonal states. However, this technique frequently requires inverting norm matrices that are ill-conditioned, making them highly vulnerable to noise. This vulnerability is particularly acute when matrix elements are computed via stochastic methods, resulting in significant error bars. To address this, we present the trimmed sampling algorithm, which markedly mitigates noise effects. Leveraging Bayesian inference, the algorithm samples prior probability distributions for the Hamiltonian and norm matrices, incorporating physics-informed constraints regarding the norm matrix's positivity and the convergence of extremal eigenvalues relative to subspace dimensions. The resulting output provides a probability distribution for eigenvectors and observables, complete with a robust error estimate, outperforming standard regularization techniques. Consequently, this method holds immediate potential for diverse applications spanning both classical and quantum computing.

Music time structure inference offers diverse applications across production, processing, and analysis. Researchers have developed various techniques to examine temporal elements like beat, downbeat, tempo, and meter. However, many current state-of-the-art approaches are computationally intensive, rendering them unsuitable for industrial environments that handle music collections in the millions. This paper introduces a novel state space and semi-Markov model designed for music time structure analysis. By employing a jump-back reward strategy, the method converts the standard 2D state spaces into a 1D model, drastically reducing their size. The proposed technique is applied to jointly track causal beats, downbeats, tempo, and meter, with results compared against existing methods. It achieves performance comparable to leading state-of-the-art joint causal models while utilizing a significantly smaller state space and delivering over a 30-fold increase in speed.

The quality of learned clusters in clustering algorithms heavily depends on the selection of initial centers. This paper introduces a novel initialization method, termed HST initialization, specifically for the $k$-median problem within general metric spaces, such as graph-induced discrete spaces. This approach leverages the construction of a metric embedding tree structure from the data. Based on this tree, we propose an efficient search algorithm to identify high-quality initial centers, which are then utilized by a local search algorithm. Our HST initialization yields initial centers with lower error rates compared to the popular $k$-median++ method, while maintaining comparable efficiency. Furthermore, the HST initialization can be adapted to differential privacy (DP) settings to produce private initial centers. We demonstrate that applying DP local search combined with our private HST initialization improves upon existing approximation error results and approaches the lower bound within a small factor. Experimental results validate our theoretical findings and confirm the method's effectiveness. Additionally, our approach is extendable to the $k$-means problem.

This paper investigates the viability of deploying drones for single-payload deliveries from a depot to a customer by addressing the Mission-Feasibility Problem (MFP). To handle the dynamic nature of deliveries under payload limitations, we introduce a novel framework utilizing time-dependent cost graphs. Specifically, we account for variable global winds that alter energy consumption during flight, which is modeled by adjusting edge costs in the graph. We propose three algorithms to manage these dynamics: (i) calculating an initial minimum-energy route, (ii) dynamically re-evaluating the optimal path to the destination, and (iii) dynamically selecting the best local option. These algorithms operate with partial information, receiving updated edge costs only when the drone traverses a new vertex, rather than knowing future weights in advance. We assess their performance using both synthetic and real-world datasets, comparing outcomes based on three categories: successful missions (delivery and return to depot), partial successes (delivery achieved but return failed), and total failures (neither delivery nor return achieved).

While single-domain magnetic nanoparticles can be effectively switched by a linear down-chirp microwave field pulse (DCMWP) at zero temperature, real-world applications inevitably involve finite temperatures. This study investigates the impact of such temperatures on DCMWP-induced magnetization reversal using the stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. Our results indicate that when temperature rises, one of the three key DCMWP parameters—amplitude, chirp rate, or initial frequency—must be reduced while the other two remain constant. Furthermore, the maximum temperature allowing for reversal increases as the system size grows. These trends stem from the fact that anisotropy-induced energy barriers scale with system volume, whereas effective magnetization diminishes with higher temperatures. Additionally, we present a set of optimized parameters for practical implementation. These insights offer a pathway to achieving rapid, low-cost magnetization reversal across a broad operating temperature range.

Automated categorization of human anatomy serves as a crucial foundation for numerous computer-aided diagnostic systems. However, the inherent spatial variability and complexity of human anatomy present significant challenges for classification. In image classification tasks, deep learning techniques, particularly convolutional neural networks (ConvNets), have demonstrated superior performance compared to other state-of-the-art methods. This study introduces a ConvNet-based approach designed for classifying medical images obtained via computed tomography (CT) into specific organ or body-part categories. The model was trained on 4,298 distinct axial 2D key-images representing five anatomical classes, which were extracted from a hospital PACS archive containing data from 1,675 patients. Our results indicate that data augmentation techniques can effectively expand the dataset and enhance classification accuracy. By leveraging ConvNets alongside data augmentation, we achieved a classification error rate of 5.9% and an average area-under-the-curve (AUC) of 0.998 during testing. These findings demonstrate that deep learning can produce highly reliable and accurate classifiers capable of serving as robust initializers for further computer-aided diagnosis applications.

This study investigates LaAlO$_3$/Eu$_{1-x}$La$_x$TiO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ heterostructures with nominal x values of 0 and 0.1 across varying Eu$_{1-x}$La$_x$TiO$_3$ layer thicknesses. We find that these systems exhibit numerous characteristics akin to previously examined LaAlO$_3$/EuTiO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ interfaces and similar oxide junctions, including the generation of a two-dimensional electron liquid for 1–2 unit cells of Eu$_{1-x}$La$_x$TiO$_3$, a metal-insulator transition induced by increasing the Eu$_{1-x}$La$_x$TiO$_3$ thickness, an Anomalous Hall effect (AHE) emerging above the Lifshitz point via backgate voltage, and a distinct minimum in sheet resistance temperature dependence below the Lifshitz point within the one-band regime, which intensifies with higher gate voltages. Despite the probable presence of magnetism, we do not ascribe this resistance minimum to the Kondo effect; instead, we attribute it to the intrinsic properties of the SrTiO$_3$ crystal and unavoidable charge trapping effects associated with backgating.

We present a theoretical analysis of an advanced experimental technique combining electron spin resonance and scanning tunneling microscopy (ESR-STM) to directly investigate spin fluctuations within the Kondo effect. In this setup, the Kondo impurity is exchange-coupled to a probe spin, allowing the ESR-STM apparatus to detect minute level shifts in the probe spin caused by the impurity's spin fluctuations. By employing the open quantum system framework—treating the probe spin as the "system" and the Kondo impurity as the fluctuating "bath"—we calculate resonance line shifts based on the impurity's dynamic spin susceptibility. We examine various common surface adatoms as potential probe spins to estimate their respective level shifts, finding that sensitivity is maximized when the probe spins possess transverse magnetic anisotropy.

In recent years, investment choices have increasingly prioritized issues like climate change and human rights, prompting investors—both asset managers and owners—to evaluate companies based on their management of these topics. To facilitate this, investors depend on specialized rating agencies that assign scores across environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria, aiding decisions aligned with sustainability. However, these agencies rely on subjective analyses of sustainability reports, which not all companies provide. Additionally, the manual nature of their work hinders timely scaling of coverage. To address these limitations and further support sustainability, we introduce a heterogeneous ensemble model that predicts ESG ratings using fundamental data. This approach combines feedforward neural networks with CatBoost and XGBoost. Since fundamental data is publicly accessible, our method enables cost-effective and scalable generation of initial ESG ratings, even for firms lacking sustainability reports. Our model explains 54% of rating variation (R²) using fundamental data, outperforming previous efforts in the field.

This work investigates Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) techniques for approximating the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. Specifically, we examine a scenario where the nonlinear term is discretized differently in the snapshots (generated via a full-order method, or FOM) than in the POD reduction. We demonstrate that this discrepancy introduces an additional error term absent when identical discretizations are used for both methods; however, this term is of the same magnitude as the FOM error, meaning the POD convergence rate remains largely unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of incorporating grad-div stabilization into both the FOM and POD frameworks, which yields error bounds with constants independent of inverse viscosity powers, alongside a study of the unstabilized case. Theoretical findings are corroborated by numerical experiments.

This study presents a suite of numerical techniques for analyzing 3D surface shapes on Riemannian manifolds using invariant, elastic second-order Sobolev metrics. Specifically, we focus on calculating geodesics and geodesic distances between parametrized or unparametrized immersed surfaces modeled as 3D meshes. Leveraging these computations, we create tools for statistical shape analysis of surface collections, including methods for estimating Karcher means, conducting tangent PCA on shape populations, and calculating parallel transport along surface paths. Our method is grounded in a relaxed variational approach to the geodesic matching problem, utilizing varifold fidelity terms. This framework ensures reparametrization independence when computing geodesics between unparametrized surfaces and provides versatile algorithms capable of comparing surfaces with different sampling densities or mesh structures. Furthermore, we show how this relaxed variational framework can be adapted to handle partially observed data. The advantages of our numerical pipeline are demonstrated through various synthetic and real-world examples.

Monitoring human fertility for natural conception or assisted reproductive technologies has long posed a significant challenge for both clinicians and patients. While human eggs become fertilizable upon reaching the Fallopian tubes from the upper reproductive tract, no existing technology has yet been able to independently detect the presence of these eggs, alert medical staff and patients in real time to initiate subsequent procedures promptly. This paper introduces a conceptual architecture grounded in communications engineering principles. The proposed system integrates an intra-body nano-sensor network to monitor Fallopian tube activity with a body-area network that receives this data and transmits it wirelessly to physicians, nurses, and patients. Preliminary simulations using a particle-based stochastic simulator examined the interplay between achievable information rates, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and distance. Results indicate that data rates up to 300 Mbps are feasible at an SNR of 45. Consequently, this architecture guarantees near-zero latency and minimal energy consumption with high throughput, ensuring that critical actions can be executed within the brief window of Fallopian tube activity.

This work defines and examines the characteristics of contact Lie systems, which are first-order differential equations whose integral curves correspond to a time-dependent vector field within a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of Hamiltonian vector fields defined under a contact structure. Specifically, we investigate families of conservative contact Lie systems. We establish and apply Liouville theorems, contact reductions, and Gromov non-squeezing theorems to these systems. The findings are demonstrated through examples with significant physical and mathematical relevance, such as the Schwarz equations and Brockett systems.

Cell size expansion is a sophisticated mechanism governed by both internal and external cues. Recent research [Tzur et al., Science, 2009, 325:167-171] analyzed size distributions within exponentially expanding mammalian cell populations to deduce growth rates, concluding that growth follows neither a linear nor exponential pattern but is instead regulated by cell size. To account for these findings, we developed a model where growth velocity depends on the ratio of mRNA to ribosomes within the cell. By integrating this with a stochastic division mechanism, we simulated the evolution of cell populations; the statistical outcomes of our in-silico experiments align closely with empirical data. We further investigated alternative growth frameworks and division strategies to explore the broader model space. Ultimately, this study offers a foundational approach for elucidating the logic behind cell growth and size control through predictive modeling.

Three major discrepancies from Standard Model predictions—specifically the elevated decay rate of B $	o$ D$^{(*)}	au
u$, potential lepton universality violations in B $	o$ K$^{(*)}\ell\ell$ decays, and the anomalous muon magnetic moment—can be accounted for by leptoquarks (LQs) that strongly couple to third-generation quarks and possess TeV-scale masses. These hypothetical particles can be investigated at the LHC through high-energy proton-proton collisions. This study introduces a new search for leptoquark pair production involving top quarks and muons, utilizing 35.9 fb$^{-1}$ of data collected by the CMS experiment at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. No significant deviations from Standard Model expectations were found, leading to the exclusion of scalar LQs decaying solely into t$\mu$ pairs up to a mass of 1420 GeV. By combining these findings with prior searches for LQ decays into t$	au$ and b$
u$, which ruled out scalar LQs below 900 and 1080 GeV respectively, the analysis excludes vector LQs up to 1190 GeV across all branching fraction combinations of t$\mu$, t$	au$, and b$
u$. Consequently, this analysis marks the first-time probing of all relevant couplings for leptoquarks with an electric charge of -1/3 interacting with third-generation quarks.

The prevalence of drug-resistant bacteria, prions, and nosocomial infections highlights the urgent requirement for more efficient sterilization methods, for which cold plasma technology offers a promising solution. An evaluation was conducted on six distinct printed circuit board-based plasma sources, each tested four times. This assessment included measurements of power consumption, ignition dynamics captured by an ICCD camera, and ozone generation quantified via absorption spectroscopy at 254 nm. To assess biocidal efficacy, four test series were executed using *Escherichia coli*, covering the entire spectrum from input parameters to the resulting inactivation of pathogens. Discharge current and time-resolved ignition data revealed that filaments form simultaneously at the start of the negative half-cycle. Ozone production dynamics exhibited saturated exponential growth, peaking at 435 ppm. Microbiological tests further demonstrated performance variations among the different plasma source designs. A total reduction rate of Log-4 was achieved within one minute. However, air flow through slits in the plasma sources destabilized the discharge, and minor adjustments to electrode geometry altered all measured parameters. Consequently, these findings recommend a comb-shaped electrode design laminated onto a dielectric as the optimal approach for developing effective pathogen-inactivating plasma sources.

When humans define cost or goal parameters for robots, the resulting specifications are frequently ambiguous, incomplete, or unsolvable by standard planners.
