Experiments across multiple cross-domain benchmarks, including Office-31, Office-Home, CUB-Paintings, and Duke-Market-1510, demonstrate that EvoADA consistently enhances various state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods, with optimal attention configurations yielding superior performance.

Currently, a wide array of paid online services, such as video streaming, ride-sharing, and event ticketing, require users to authenticate via credentials linked to their identities after registration. Similarly, physical services like attending concerts involve receiving a ticket that validates the user's entitlement to the service. Both models suffer from centralization and fail to adequately protect user privacy, as Service Providers act as Trusted Third Parties managing sensitive data. This paper introduces FORT, a decentralized framework enabling users to verify their right to access services—digital or physical—without disclosing private information. To ensure decentralization, all data is managed on a Blockchain. User rights are uniquely defined using Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs), while privacy is guaranteed through Zero-Knowledge Proofs, cryptographic methods that allow proof of possession without revealing underlying data. Additionally, performance benchmarks demonstrate that FORT is sufficiently efficient for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as smartphones and smartwatches, which are typical in this use case.

We introduce a protocol for creating multi-particle entangled states through the coherent control of atoms confined within an optical cavity. By utilizing two control beams and leveraging interactions mediated by the cavity, we demonstrate the adiabatic generation of entanglement. This approach facilitates optimal entanglement production for the specific measurement scheme we outline. We examine a potential experimental realization and compare the performance of our generated states against both classical states and ideal maximally-entangled Dicke states. Our findings indicate that these states consistently offer metrological advantages, surpassing even ideal Dicke states in the measurement of magnetic field gradients. Given the protocol's inherent scalability, it represents a promising avenue for quantum state engineering.

When addressing multi-objective optimization problems through scalarization methods, the resulting solutions are typically weakly efficient rather than fully efficient with respect to the original problem. Therefore, it is essential to identify the conditions under which the weakly efficient set coincides with the efficient set. This paper provides such a characterization, assuming the convexity of the free disposal hull of the domain. Leveraging this result, we derive several mathematical applications. In a practical context, we demonstrate that all weakly efficient solutions to a slightly modified multi-objective LASSO problem are indeed efficient.

We demonstrate that a sound mode existing at zero temperature in certain holographic systems with global U(1) symmetry—arising without spontaneous symmetry breaking or Fermi surface formation—also appears in zero-density holographic quantum critical states. In these systems, the emergence of this mode stems from a mixed 't Hooft anomaly between the global U(1) symmetry and an emergent higher-form symmetry. At non-zero temperatures, the black hole horizon induces a weak breaking of this emergent symmetry, which gaps the collective mode and produces a sharp Drude-like peak in electric conductivity. Similarly, at low but non-zero temperatures, states possessing emergent Lorentz symmetry exhibit a gapped mode derived from an approximate anomalous higher-form symmetry; however, unlike the zero-density case, this excitation fails to persist at zero temperature and instead dissolves into a branch cut. We also discuss the implications of these findings for applying the Luttinger theorem to compressible holographic matter.

This paper investigates composition operators acting on Harmonic-Bloch type spaces, calculates their spectra, and identifies the conditions under which these operators are isometric on harmonic Bloch type spaces.

This work examines cell colorings for graph drawings on a plane. For a multi-graph $G$ and its planar drawing $\Gamma(G)$ containing a finite number of crossings, a cell $k$-coloring assigns $k$ colors to the maximal connected regions (cells) such that no two adjacent cells share the same color. According to the Four Color Theorem, any drawing of a bridgeless graph possesses a cell 4-coloring. Furthermore, a graph drawing is cell 2-colorable precisely when its underlying graph is Eulerian. We demonstrate that every graph lacking vertices of degree 1 admits a drawing that is cell 3-colorable. This finding prompts the inquiry into which abstract graphs guarantee a cell 3-coloring for every possible drawing; such graphs are termed universally cell 3-colorable. We establish that all 4-edge-connected graphs and those admitting a nowhere-zero 3-flow are universally cell 3-colorable. Additionally, we explore conditions where universal cell 3-colorability implies the existence of a nowhere-zero 3-flow. Conversely, we identify an infinite family of graphs that are universally cell 3-colorable yet lack a nowhere-zero 3-flow. On a positive note, we propose a conjecture with a notable connection to Tutte's famous open 3-flow conjecture, which we prove holds for subcubic graphs and graphs free of $K_{3,3}$ minors.

The emergence of discrete breather excitations across diverse media relies fundamentally on nonlinearity and discreteness. We contend that the forced ferromagnetic phase of the monoaxial chiral helimagnet CrNb$_3$S$_6$ satisfies these conditions through its unique domain architecture. In this system, stationary, time-periodic breather modes manifest as discrete breather lattice solutions where the mode period does not align with the system size. Driven by the intrinsic easy-plane single-ion anisotropy of CrNb$_3$S$_6$, these modes exhibit dark characteristics, with frequencies situated within the linear spin-wave band near its lower boundary. These states represent magnetization cnoidal waves, analogous to the established soliton lattice ground state, but featuring a finite, variable number of embedded $2\pi$-kinks. The linear stability of these dark breather modes has been confirmed via Floquet analysis. Furthermore, their energy, governed by the breather lattice period and amplitude, decreases linearly as the number of kinks increases. These findings could open new avenues for designing spintronic resonators utilizing chiral helimagnets.

Gaussian processes offer a flexible approach to learning unknown functions by incorporating prior knowledge about their characteristics. While numerous Gaussian process models exist for Euclidean input spaces, options for undirected graph inputs are significantly more restricted. This study utilizes the stochastic partial differential equation formulation of Mat\'ern Gaussian processes—a popular model in Euclidean contexts—to develop their corresponding analogs for undirected graphs. We demonstrate that these graph-based processes retain key advantageous properties found in their Euclidean and Riemannian counterparts and introduce methods for training them via standard techniques like inducing points. Consequently, graph Mat\'ern Gaussian processes can now be applied in mini-batch and non-conjugate scenarios, enhancing their accessibility for practitioners and facilitating their integration into broader learning systems.

While retouching greatly enhances photo aesthetics, amateur photographers often lack the professional skills required to execute it effectively. A particularly difficult aspect of restoring old images involves eliminating dust and scratches; traditionally, this has been a laborious manual process relying on specialized software and expert knowledge. However, recent studies have demonstrated that Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) yield superior results in automated image enhancement compared to conventional techniques. This has inspired our investigation into applying GANs specifically to film photo restoration. We introduce a GAN-based approach designed to eradicate dust and scratches from film scans, leveraging residual learning to accelerate training and improve denoising efficacy. Comprehensive testing on a community-sourced dataset reveals that our model generalizes exceptionally well across diverse image types without relying on specific characteristics. Ultimately, our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art software and techniques, delivering superior restoration quality.

Families of Bridgeland stability conditions generate corresponding families of stability data, wall-crossing structures, and scattering diagrams on the motivic Hall algebra. When the stability conditions within a family possess a global dimension of at most 2, these structures can be transferred to the quantum torus. We demonstrate that geometric stability conditions on surfaces with nef anticanonical bundles have a global dimension of 2 and analyze the resulting family of stability data. Furthermore, we propose a conjecture linking this family to the stability data family associated with a quiver with potential, and we confirm this conjecture specifically for the projective plane.

The classical sharp threshold theorem by Friedgut and Kalai (1996) states that every symmetric monotone function $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}$ displays a sharp threshold phenomenon. This indicates that the expectation of $f$ under the biased measure $\mu_{p}$ rises swiftly from 0 to 1 as $p$ grows. In this work, we introduce "robust" variants of this theorem, demonstrating that the phenomenon persists even when the function is "almost" monotone and satisfies a significantly weaker form of symmetry. Contrary to the original proof, which depends on hypercontractivity, our approach utilizes a "regularity" lemma—related to Szemerédi's regularity lemma and its extensions—and the "invariance principle" by Mossel, O'Donnell, and Oleszkiewicz. This principle permits, under specific conditions, the substitution of functions defined on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^{n}$ with those on Gaussian random variables.

Gowers (2007) and independently Nagle, Rödl, Schacht, and Skokan (2006) established the hypergraph removal lemma, which posits that if a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains a sparse number of copies of a fixed hypergraph $H$, then removing a small number of edges renders it $H$-free. Although this resolves the "hypergraph removal problem" for fixed $k$ and $H$, the result becomes ineffective when $k$ is large (for instance, when $k>\log\log\log n$). By applying our robust extension of the Friedgut-Kalai theorem, we derive a hypergraph removal lemma applicable to $k$ values linear in $n$ for a broad class of hypergraphs. This class includes all hypergraphs where both the total number of edges and the sizes of pairwise edge intersections are bounded by a constant.

In a high-dimensional framework where both the data dimension and sample size grow proportionally to infinity, we establish a central limit theorem (CLT) for the linear spectral statistics (LSS) of large-dimensional sample covariance matrices. Unlike prior studies, our findings do not necessitate the assumption that population covariance matrices are bounded. Furthermore, the proposed approach accommodates many common kernel functions found in real-world data, including logarithmic and polynomial functions. Within our model, the count of spiked eigenvalues may remain fixed or increase without bound. A key characteristic of the asymptotic mean and covariance in our derived CLT is their dependence on the divergence order of the population spectral norm.

This research examines behavioral shifts within the dynamic healthcare system and their impact on decision-making. We employ Evolutionary Game Theory to identify the most likely strategies adopted by individuals in a finite population based on their interactions. Our modeling approach incorporates specific metrics, including investment costs, management costs, treatment costs, provider reputation gains, and patient health outcomes.

This study investigates the circular trajectories and polarized imaging of charged particles orbiting a Kerr black hole within a weak magnetic field. We focus specifically on scenarios where both the magnetic field strength and the charge-to-mass ratio are small; under these conditions, the effective potential for radial motion approximates a cubic form, allowing for an analytical expression of the innermost stable circular orbit radius as a function of the particles' energy and angular momentum. Furthermore, we calculated the polarized synchrotron radiation from these particles and derived semi-analytical polarized images across different black hole spins, viewing angles, and both prograde and retrograde orbits. Notably, we determined that these parameters exert a substantial influence on both the magnitude of the polarization flux and the rotation of polarization.

The capacity of a linear attenuating optical channel, where the signal is regenerated using quantum-limited phase-sensitive amplifiers, is examined across both conventional and generalized detection frameworks. Furthermore, the continuous model of distributed amplification establishes the achievable capacity for long-haul links subject to a total power constraint.

Fifth-generation (5G) mobile communication technology is poised to become the next standard for mobile networking, making it timely to evaluate its influence on the computing landscape, specifically regarding data management and data-driven innovations. Anticipating bandwidth increases of 10 to 100 times and latency reductions of 5 to 10 times, 5G is expected to serve as the primary catalyst for edge computing. This includes facilitating access to cloud-like services and enabling machine learning at the edge. This paper investigates the effects of 5G on both established and emerging technologies while outlining associated research challenges and opportunities.

Drawing from homological idelic class field theory, we establish an analogue of the Hilbert reciprocity law for a rational homology 3-sphere equipped with an infinite link, aligning with the principles of arithmetic topology. In this framework, the intersection form on the unitary normal bundle of each knot serves as the counterpart to the Hilbert symbol at a prime ideal, thereby enabling the formulation of the reciprocity law and ensuring that cyclic link covers correspond to Kummer extensions.

The Nikaidō-Isoda-Fan inequality defines an equilibrium problem that encompasses several well-known problems—including optimization, variational inequalities, Kakutani fixed points, and Nash equilibria—as specific instances. This paper illustrates the connection between the fixed points of the Moreau proximal mapping and the solutions to the equilibrium problem, under certain monotonicity and Lipschitz-type conditions.

This work establishes sharp large deviation results of the Bahadur-Ranga Rao type for the $q$-norms of random vectors distributed on the $\ell_p^n$-ball $\mathbb{B}^n_p$ under either a cone probability measure or a uniform distribution, valid for $1 \le q < p < \infty$. These findings extend prior large deviation analyses by Kabluchko, Prochno, and Thäle within the same framework. Subsequently, these results are utilized to derive sharp asymptotics for the intersection volumes of distinct $\ell_p^n$-balls, following the approach of Schechtman and Schmuckenschläger, as well as for the length of the projection of an $\ell_p^n$-ball onto a line with a uniformly random direction. The proofs of these sharp large deviation results rely on constructing convenient probabilistic representations of the $q$-norms, applying local limit theorems to approximate their densities, and leveraging geometric results on the asymptotic expansions of Laplace integrals to integrate these densities and obtain precise probability estimates.

Seagrasses play a critical role in coastal ecosystems, yet their rapid population decline over recent decades raises significant concerns for marine health. Spatial models offer a mathematical approach to examine the dynamics and collective behaviors of seagrass meadows, serving as essential tools for forecasting responses to global warming, assessing ecosystem resilience, and refining restoration efforts. This article introduces a model grounded in plant clonal growth rules that accounts for interactions between different seagrass species. We provide a theoretical analysis focusing on the specific interaction between the seagrass *Cymodocea nodosa* and the seaweed *Caulerpa prolifera*. Our simulations effectively replicate field data regarding shoot densities in mixed meadows located in the Mediterranean Sea's Ebro River Delta. Furthermore, this model enables the exploration of potential mechanisms driving interactions among macrophytes.

This paper introduces a novel estimation technique for the blind source separation framework presented by Bachoc et al. (2020). The approach utilizes eigenanalysis of a positive definite matrix constructed from several normalized spatial local covariance matrices, enabling the handling of moderately high-dimensional random fields. We establish the consistency of the estimated mixing matrix with explicit error bounds, even in scenarios where the eigen-gap diminishes gradually. Furthermore, the method's efficacy is demonstrated through both simulation studies and an application to real-world data.

Euler's equations describe the dynamics of gravity waves on the surface of an incompressible, inviscid, and irrotational fluid with any depth. This study examines the spectral stability of sufficiently small-amplitude, one-dimensional Stokes waves—defined as periodic gravity waves maintaining a permanent form and constant velocity—in both finite and infinite depths. By employing a nonlocal formulation of Euler's equations introduced by Ablowitz et al. (2006), we construct a perturbation method to characterize the initial high-frequency instabilities located away from the origin within the spectrum of the linearization around these small-amplitude Stokes waves. For the first time, asymptotic and numerical calculations of these instabilities are presented, demonstrating excellent agreement.

Ram-pressure stripping by the intracluster medium (ICM) is a leading mechanism influencing cluster galaxy properties. While a recent study on a small sample suggested a correlation between this stripping and the presence of active galactic nuclei (AGN), a subsequent investigation failed to confirm this link. To address this, we utilized MUSE observations from the GASP program alongside a comprehensive literature review to robustly determine the AGN fraction in ram-pressure stripped galaxies using BPT emission line diagrams. Analyzing a sample of 115 stripped galaxies with stellar masses $\geq 10^9 \, M_{\odot}$, we identified an AGN fraction of approximately 27%. However, this fraction is heavily dependent on stellar mass, increasing to 51% when restricted to galaxies with $M_* \geq 10^{10} \, M_{\odot}$. Furthermore, comparing mass-matched samples of stripped cluster galaxies against non-cluster galaxies from the MaNGA survey, we found that AGN activity is significantly more prevalent during active ram-pressure stripping (with a confidence level $>99.95\%$), thereby supporting the hypothesis of a connection between AGN and ram pressure.

Light can initiate the motion of a mechanically compliant element, which subsequently induces ponderomotive correlations within the electromagnetic field. While optomechanical cavities typically amplify these correlations to achieve quantum squeezing of light, observing such effects in free-space setups—where no cavity is present—has historically been difficult due to weak interactions and remains unreported. In this study, we successfully measured a ponderomotively squeezed state of light scattered by a nanoparticle suspended in a free-space optical tweezer. We detected a decrease in optical fluctuations by as much as 25% below the vacuum level across a bandwidth of approximately 15 kHz. These findings align well with a linearized dipole interaction model between the nanoparticle and the electromagnetic continuum. The resulting ponderomotive correlations pave the way for quantum-enhanced sensing and metrology using levitated systems, enabling force measurements that surpass the standard quantum limit.

This study investigates the current algebras associated with NS5-branes, Kaluza-Klein (KK) five-branes, and the exotic $5^2_2$-branes within type IIA/IIB superstring theories. The dynamics of these branes' worldvolume theories are dictated by six-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ tensor multiplets and $\mathcal{N}=(1,1)$ vector multiplets. We demonstrate that these current algebras arise from S- and T-dualities. Specifically, the algebras for $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ theories are defined by Dirac brackets resulting from the self-dual gauge field on the five-brane worldvolumes, whereas those for $\mathcal{N}=(1,1)$ theories are described by Poisson brackets. Utilizing these algebraic structures, we analyze extended spaces via tensor coordinates representing ten-dimensional supersymmetry and investigate the transformation rules of currents within the ten-dimensional type IIA/IIB supersymmetry algebras. Furthermore, based on these algebras, we formulate the section conditions for the extended spaces and derive the gauge transformations for supergravity fields.

PSR J1813–1749 is a particularly intriguing object due to its unique characteristics. It ranks among the most energetic and widely scattered pulsars and is linked to HESS J1813–178, one of the sky's brightest and most compact TeV emitters. Ho et al. recently analyzed archival Chandra X-ray data spanning over a decade, finding a total proper motion of approximately 66 mas yr⁻¹. At a distance of 6.2 kpc, this implies a velocity of roughly 1900 km s⁻¹, suggesting the pulsar is the fastest known neutron star in the Galaxy. Based on its angular separation from the supernova remnant's center, Ho et al. estimated an age of only ~300 years, marking it as one of the youngest pulsars. However, by utilizing 12 years of high-angular-resolution VLA observations, we determined that the radio proper motion of PSR J1813–1748 is significantly lower: (μα·cos δ, μδ) = (−5.0±3.7, −13.2±6.7) mas yr⁻¹, resulting in a total proper motion of 14.8±5.9 mas yr⁻¹. Since our positions are referenced against quasars, these findings are reliable. Consequently, we conclude that PSR J1813–1749 is not a high-velocity source. Using this new proper motion, its kinematic age is calculated to be ~1350 years. This estimate aligns within a factor of a few with the pulsar's characteristic age, the broadband spectral energy distribution age of HESS J1813–178, and the age of the associated supernova remnant.

This article introduces novel techniques for demonstrating convex semialgebraic sets that cannot be represented as spectrahedral shadows. We establish a characterization for when the set of nonnegative polynomials with a specific support forms a spectrahedral shadow, expressed through the lens of sums of squares. Leveraging this finding, we demonstrate that the cone of copositive matrices for dimensions $n\geq5$ is not a spectrahedral shadow, thereby resolving a query posed by Scheiderer. Our methodology relies on a model-theoretic insight: any formula defining a spectrahedral shadow must remain invariant under every unital $\mathbb{R}$-linear completely positive map $R\to R$ defined on a real closed field extension $R$ of $\mathbb{R}$.

While the conventional Hartree-Fock approach to the Hubbard model relies on eigenstates of the electron number operator, this method lacks uniqueness. An alternative, inequivalent formulation utilizes Nambu two-component spinors and is grounded in eigenstates representing the difference between spin-up and spin-down electron counts; this version incorporates parameters $U$, $t$, $t'$, and the chemical potential $\mu$ to determine electron density. A primary benefit of this Nambu framework is the direct computation of electron pairing condensates. We demonstrate that within this "Nambu" Hartree-Fock approximation, low-lying states near half-filling exhibit spontaneous breaking of discrete rotation symmetry, resulting in condensates with the anticipated d-wave momentum-space structure. Furthermore, a d-wave-like symmetry can be derived analytically at $U=0$ using basic degenerate perturbation theory. At $U=0$ and half-filling, the ground states of both the Nambu and standard Hartree-Fock approaches share identical energy. However, for $U > 0$, the relative energy depends on $U$, $t'$, and electron density. Specifically, there exists a significant parameter regime where $t' > 0$ and the system is below half-filling in which the Nambu Hartree-Fock state—and its associated d-wave condensation—possesses lower energy.

We propose a new approach for examining quantum forces within a cavity, applicable to both free scalar and free fermionic fields. By employing a generalized Matsubara procedure, we calculate the quantum pressure exerted on the boundaries of a compactified space immersed in a thermal bath. Furthermore, by analyzing both periodic and antiperiodic boundary conditions, we explore whether the resulting quantum forces are attractive or repulsive. Our findings underscore the significance and interdisciplinary potential of the generalized Matsubara procedure as a theoretical framework for addressing quantum phenomena in complex topologies.

This work addresses inverse maximum theorems, drawing inspiration from contributions by Aoyama, Komiya, Li et al., Park and Komiya, and Yamauchi. Our findings lead to the statement and proof of an inverse maximum Nash theorem, demonstrating that, under appropriate conditions, any generalized Nash game can be transformed into a classical Nash game. Furthermore, we establish that the Arrow-Debreu result regarding the existence of solutions for generalized Nash games is equivalent to the Debreu-Fan-Glicksberg theorem for classical Nash games, which itself corresponds to Kakutani-Fan-Glicksberg's fixed point theorem.

A coarse space $X$ is defined as linearly ordered when it possesses a linear order compatible with its coarse structure. We demonstrate that every such linearly ordered coarse space $X$ is locally convex and possesses an asymptotic dimension of either $0$ or $1$. Furthermore, if $X$ is metrizable, then the collection of all right bounded subsets of $X$ admits a selector.

The physical nature of circumstellar envelopes (CSE) surrounding Cepheid variables remains controversial, with their infrared (IR) excess potentially arising from an ionized gas shell, a dust envelope, or a combination of both. This research seeks to define the geometry and IR excess of the long-period Cepheid $\ell$ Car (period = 35.5 days) at mid-infrared wavelengths to clarify its physical composition. The study initially employs multi-band photometry and Spitzer Space Telescope spectroscopy to limit the IR excess of $\ell$ Car. Subsequently, VLTI/MATISSE measurements taken at a specific observational phase are analyzed to determine the size, shape, and flux contribution of the stellar environment in the L band. Finally, the hypothesis of an ionized gas shell is tested to model the observed IR excess. The authors report the first L-band detection of a centro-symmetric extended emission around $\ell$ Car, measuring approximately 1.7$R_\star$ in FWHM and generating an excess of roughly 7.0%. Conversely, VLTI/MATISSE correlated flux and Spitzer data show no definitive evidence for dust emission in the N band. In contrast, a modeled ionized gas shell suggests a more compact CSE ($1.13\pm0.02\,R_\star$) with a fainter IR excess of 1% in the L band. These findings provide new evidence for a compact CSE around $\ell$ Car and demonstrate the utility of VLTI/MATISSE in characterizing common CSE properties. Although the compact CSE is likely gaseous, the tested ionized gas shell model fails to simultaneously reproduce both the IR excess and interferometric data. Further VLTI/MATISSE observations of Galactic Cepheids are required to determine CSE properties, which may vary based on pulsation period and evolutionary state.

Machine learning models undergo updates when new data becomes available or novel architectures emerge. While these updates typically enhance performance, they can inadvertently cause backward compatibility issues, negatively impacting specific users or groups. A similar challenge arises when training datasets fail to accurately represent population demographics, leading to underrepresentation of certain groups and raising significant fairness concerns. This study investigates how concepts from distributional robustness and minimax fairness can improve backward compatibility in such contexts and introduces two methods to tackle this problem directly. Our theoretical findings are supported by experimental results using the CIFAR-10, CelebA, and Waterbirds image classification datasets. The code is available at github.com/natalialmg/GroupBC.

The $\alpha$-cluster structure within the $^{48}$Ti nucleus has been demonstrated for the first time, a finding that is crucial for assessing the half-life of neutrinoless double-$\beta$ decay ($0\nu\beta\beta$) in $^{48}$Ca. A comprehensive framework unifying scattering and structural properties was applied to the $\alpha$+$^{44}$Ca system. Utilizing a global potential that accurately models experimental $\alpha$+$^{44}$Ca scattering across incident energies ($E_\alpha$) from 18 to 100 MeV, the study successfully describes the observed fusion excitation function for the $\alpha$+$^{44}$Ca system at $E_\alpha$ between 9 and 18 MeV. Specifically, the resonance peak at $E_\alpha$=10.2 MeV is attributed to a $7^-$ state within the higher nodal band, exhibiting $\alpha$+$^{44}$Ca cluster structure in $^{48}$Ti. Furthermore, the local potential $\alpha$+$^{44}$Ca cluster model positions the ground band of $^{48}$Ti consistent with experimental data and effectively reproduces the enhanced $B(E2)$ values in this band. These results indicate that collectivity arising from $\alpha$ clustering in $^{48}$Ti must be incorporated into calculations of the nuclear matrix element for the $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay of $^{48}$Ca.

Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) serves as a neuroimaging method that detects brain activity by monitoring blood oxygen levels across various regions in response to specific tasks. While fMRI data exists, the prediction of cognitive fatigue states has not been fully explored. This study addresses this gap by framing the issue as a multi-class classification task, categorizing cognitive fatigue into six distinct levels from none to extreme. We developed a spatio-temporal architecture utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for temporal modeling of 4D fMRI scans. Additionally, we employed the self-supervised Momentum Contrast (MoCo) method to pre-train our model on the public BOLD5000 dataset before fine-tuning it on our proprietary labeled data to predict fatigue levels. Our new dataset comprises fMRI scans from both Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) patients and healthy controls (HCs) undergoing N-back cognitive tasks. This approach establishes a state-of-the-art method for analyzing cognitive fatigue from fMRI data, outperforming previous solutions.

This study provides a lattice calculation of the primary corrections to nucleon and $\Delta$ resonance masses within QCD+QED, derived to first order in the isospin-breaking parameters: the electromagnetic coupling $\alpha_{EM}$ and the ratio $\frac{{\hat{m}}_d - {\hat{m}}_u}{\Lambda_{QCD}}$, which arises from the mass difference between $u$ and $d$ quarks.

The emission of an $\alpha$ particle from a nucleus is interpreted as a quantum resonance state within a two-body scattering process involving an $\alpha$ particle and a daughter nucleus, governed by a newly proposed nucleus-nucleus potential with a squared Woods-Saxon shape. Using rigorous optical model (OM) potential scattering theory based on S-matrix formalism, the validity of this potential is confirmed by its ability to accurately reproduce elastic scattering and reaction cross-section data for the $\alpha$+nucleus system. By identifying the pole positions of the S-matrix in the complex momentum ($k$) plane, the energy and width of the resonance state—corresponding to the decaying $\alpha$ emission—are determined. These parameters allow for the calculation of $\alpha$-decay half-lives, which align with experimental results across a wide range of $\alpha$-emitters, including heavy and super-heavy nuclei. Furthermore, the S-matrix derived from the full OM calculation is substituted with an analytical function constructed from exact Schrödinger solutions of a global potential; this potential effectively models the Coulomb-nuclear interaction internally and pure Coulomb waves externally. The resonant poles of this modified S-matrix in the complex momentum plane subsequently yield satisfactory predictions for $\alpha$-decay half-lives across diverse nuclear species.

This paper investigates choice functions defined on partially ordered sets that adhere to the principles of heredity and outcast. For any well-ordered sequence within a poset, we construct an associated "elementary" choice function, each of which inherently satisfies both heredity and outcast conditions. Conversely, every choice function meeting these criteria can be expressed as the union of multiple elementary choice functions. This finding extends the Aizerman-Malishevsky theorem, which describes the structure of path-independent choice functions.

This paper continues previous research on classifying contact seaweed algebras. While the preceding study demonstrated that all index-one seaweed subalgebras of $A_{n-1}=\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ are contact, we now generalize this finding to index-one subalgebras of $C_{n}=\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$. Our approach relies on constructive and combinatorial methods.

The X-ray pulsar 4U 1822-371 is a low-mass X-ray binary system featuring a neutron star that exhibits periodic X-ray pulsations. Due to the system's extreme inclination, direct thermal emission from the central object and its reflection component are theoretically obscured by the accretion disc's outer edge. Assuming accretion occurs at the Eddington limit, we analyzed non-simultaneous data from XMM-Newton and NuSTAR to examine the average broadband spectrum for signs of reflection. While no such component had previously been detected in high-inclination sources like 4U 1822-371, our analysis using two distinct reflection models—Diskline plus Pexriv and the self-consistent RfxConv—reveals significant evidence for its presence, alongside two lines linked to neutral or mildly ionized iron. The continuum spectrum is adequately described by a saturated Comptonisation model and a thermal black-body component from the cooler accretion disc. We also refined the ephemeris by incorporating two new eclipse times. Our proposed scenario suggests the source accretes at the Eddington limit with an intrinsic luminosity of $10^{38}$ erg/s, yet the observed luminosity is two orders of magnitude lower. Despite the high inclination, a reflection component is necessary to account for residuals in the iron line region and the hard spectral excess. The inner disc radius remains uncertain and model-dependent; therefore, further observations are required to validate these findings, which could provide crucial insights into this peculiar and enigmatic source.

A significant number of machine learning classification systems fail to possess competency awareness, specifically the capacity to recognize when outliers—samples distinct from and absent in the training data distribution—are presented. Detecting such outliers is practically vital as it enables the system to respond reasonably to unexpected inputs. Historically, outlier detection has been implemented as a separate module within a processing pipeline, distinct from the classification model; consequently, building a comprehensive system requires training two separate models, thereby increasing overall complexity. This paper introduces the integration of an outlier detection method directly into a classification neural network by leveraging the concept of the null space. Our proposed method, Null Space Analysis (NuSA), functions by computing and regulating the magnitude of the null space projection as data traverses the network. These projections are then used to generate a score capable of distinguishing between normal and abnormal data. Experimental results demonstrate that networks trained with NuSA maintain their classification accuracy while achieving outlier detection rates comparable to those of standard outlier detection algorithms.

Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) is a standard technique for classification and dimensionality reduction, with prior research extending it from binary to multi-class scenarios. However, applications like object detection and keyframe extraction often lack consistent instance-level labels, which are mandatory for standard LDA training. Consequently, LDA cannot be directly applied to semi-supervised classification tasks. To address this, we introduce a latent variable Fisher discriminant analysis model that relaxes the labeling requirement from the instance level to the bag level—a form of semi-supervision suitable for video-level event labels in semantic frame extraction. By integrating a data-driven prior over latent variables, our approach unifies latent variable inference and dimensionality reduction within a single Bayesian framework. Experiments on the MUSK and Corel datasets show results competitive with baseline methods. Furthermore, our method is evaluated on the challenging TRECVID MED11 dataset for semantic keyframe extraction using a human-factors ranking assessment, demonstrating that it consistently generates more semantically meaningful keyframes than existing baselines.

Many applications now digitally record various facets of human life, generating data known as Personal Digital Traces (PDTs). These traces can be leveraged to reconstruct episodic memories and link individuals to their past experiences. This capability offers diverse benefits, ranging from aiding patients with neurodegenerative conditions in recalling events to identifying recent contacts and locations through multi-source analysis—a vital tool during the current health crisis. This paper advances the integration, connection, and summarization of heterogeneous data into episodic narratives by utilizing scripts, which serve as prototypical plans for daily activities. Specifically, we introduce a matching algorithm that clusters digital traces from multiple sources into script instances (episodes) and offer a method for ranking the probability of candidate episodes. We present findings from a study utilizing real user data, demonstrating that our episode reconstruction approach 1) effectively synthesizes traces from disparate sources into coherent narratives and 2) enhances users' recollection of their past actions.

Driven by recent experimental advancements regarding the $R_{D^{(\ast)}}$ and $R_{K^{(\ast)}}$ anomalies in $B$-decays, we explore a Standard Model extension incorporating a single vector leptoquark. We investigate how lepton flavour non-universality can be realized beginning with initially universal gauge couplings. Although the unitary flavour structure arising from quark-lepton mass misalignment following $SU(2)_L$ symmetry breaking fails to satisfy strict limits from lepton flavour violating processes, we demonstrate that effectively non-unitary couplings—stemming from mixings with heavy vector-like fermions—are essential for simultaneously resolving the $R_{K^{(\ast)}}$ and $R_{D^{(\ast)}}$ anomalies. Moreover, anticipated improvements in the sensitivity of charged lepton flavour violating observables in the near future will enable the exploration of a substantial portion of the preferred parameter space within this class of vector leptoquark models.

This study examines distributed secure source coding within the framework of a common key cryptosystem. This system addresses the secrecy amplification challenge for distributed encrypted sources featuring correlated keys via post-encryption compression, a problem originally formulated and analyzed by Santoso and Oohama. We introduce a novel security criterion that is generally more stringent than the standard criterion, which relies on the upper-bound of mutual information between plaintext and ciphertext. Based on this new criterion, we derive the necessary and sufficient conditions required for the secure transmission of correlated sources.

Feature-based self-explanatory methods justify their classification decisions using human-comprehensible features, a capability that significantly enhances the trustworthiness of AI systems in medical imaging through semantic alignment with clinical knowledge. However, the high cost of annotating these features remains a critical challenge. To address this, we introduce cRedAnno, a data- and annotation-efficient approach designed for lung nodule diagnosis. By employing self-supervised contrastive learning to minimize the reliance on annotations for parameter learning and replacing end-to-end training with a two-stage process, cRedAnno drastically reduces the annotation burden. Even when trained on hundreds of nodule samples with only 1% annotated, the method achieves competitive accuracy in malignancy prediction and significantly outperforms prior works in predicting nodule attributes. Furthermore, visualization of the learned feature space demonstrates that the clustering of malignancy and nodule attributes aligns with established clinical knowledge. Our complete code is available open-source at: https://github.com/diku-dk/credanno.

We examined the tunability of structural, electronic, and magnetotransport properties in polycrystalline Sr2IrO4. The divergence between field-cooled and zero-field-cooled magnetization curves indicates that the as-prepared sample exhibits greater magnetic anisotropy than the vacuum-annealed one. Based on structural and magnetic data, the annealed sample stabilizes a canted antiferromagnetic (AFM) structure over a wider temperature range compared to the as-prepared sample. At low temperatures, both samples display a competing phase, likely of glassy nature, coexisting with the canted AFM phase; this coexistence persists up to approximately 115 K for the as-prepared sample and 70 K for the annealed one. Transport analysis shows that the Arrhenius model dominates conduction in the high-temperature region for both samples. In the intermediate range, transport is governed by variable range hopping (VRH) and the Arrhenius model for the as-prepared and annealed samples, respectively. At low temperatures, conduction occurs via Efros-Shklovskii-VRH in the as-prepared sample and standard VRH in the annealed one. Magneto-resistance measurements reveal a higher negative magneto-resistance in the annealed sample across all temperatures. Furthermore, the field dependence of magneto-resistance at 10 K suggests that the as-prepared sample hosts a coexisting glassy magnetic phase alongside the canted AFM structure, whereas this glassy phase is suppressed in the annealed sample. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical role of disorder in determining the magnetic and transport properties of this compound.

We employed detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) to examine the dynamics of blood pressure oscillations and their feedback control in rats, specifically analyzing systolic pressure time series recorded before and after a surgery that disrupts the control loop. Our findings revealed a crossover between two scaling regions for each condition, where the exponents characterize the nature and operational range of the feedback control. Furthermore, we observed evidence of adaptation in blood pressure regulation dynamics a few days following the surgical interruption of the primary feedback circuit. Leveraging the paradigm of antagonistic, bipartite (vagal and sympathetic) central nervous system action, we propose a simple model for pressure homeostasis defined as the equilibrium between two opposing nonlinear forces. This model successfully replicates the crossover patterns observed in the DFA of actual pressure signals.

This paper investigates the existence of Poisson metrics on flat vector bundles over noncompact Riemannian manifolds and examines related consequences, particularly their applications in Higgs bundles. These applications aim to extend the Corlette-Donaldson-Hitchin-Simpson nonabelian Hodge correspondence to the setting of noncompact Kähler manifolds.

To observe the topography of thin oxide films as they grow, allowing for quasi real-time analysis of their growth dynamics, we developed and incorporated an atomic force microscope (AFM) into a pulsed laser deposition (PLD) vacuum chamber. The AFM scanner and PLD target are mounted on a unified support frame, coupled with a rapid sample transfer mechanism to enable in-situ microscopy following deposition pulses. This in-situ microscope functions across temperatures from room temperature up to 700$^\circ$C and at pressures ranging from the vacuum base of 10$^{-6}$ mbar to 1 mbar, covering standard PLD conditions for oxide film growth. The system's capabilities are validated by its ability to resolve unit cell height surface steps and map surface topography under typical oxide PLD growth parameters.

Recent research has heavily explored few-shot object detection by integrating meta-learning into region-based detection architectures. Although effective, this approach is limited by (i) poor region proposals for new classes and (ii) a lack of consideration for correlations between different classes, which impedes the transfer of base-class knowledge to novel objects. To address these issues, we introduce Meta-DETR, a new few-shot detection framework that embeds correlational aggregation into the DETR architecture. Unlike traditional methods, Meta-DETR operates solely at the image level without relying on region proposals, thereby eliminating the problem of inaccurate proposals. Furthermore, it can process multiple support classes simultaneously within a single feed-forward pass. This design enables the model to capture inter-class correlations, significantly lowering misclassification rates among similar categories and improving generalization to unseen classes. Extensive experiments across various few-shot benchmarks demonstrate that Meta-DETR substantially outperforms state-of-the-art techniques. The source code will be made available at https://github.com/ZhangGongjie/Meta-DETR.

The quantum dynamics of coherent states are examined within the framework of quantum field theory using two distinct yet complementary approaches: a Taylor series expansion with respect to elapsed time and a perturbative expansion in the coupling constant via the interaction-picture formalism. A key feature of our analysis is the construction of states using the operators and vacuum of the interacting theory, bypassing the need for asymptotic particles. By focusing on a coherent state representing a spatially homogeneous field, we demonstrate that both methods effectively capture nonlinear classical dynamics alongside distinguishable quantum effects. Specifically, the time-expansion approach reveals that the initial field acceleration—marking the departure from the initial expectation value—is controlled by a tree-level potential featuring a renormalized mass and bare coupling. Conversely, the interaction-picture calculation, when adjusted, yields the nonlinear dynamics defined by renormalized mass and coupling, but produces a logarithmic singularity in the initial-time field acceleration for specific initial fluctuation states, a behavior analogous to findings in semi-classical formalisms. Within our coherent-state framework, these anomalies are identified as artifacts of the respective expansions: one over infinitesimal time and the other over the coupling constant. Nevertheless, we establish that the evolution derived from the interaction-picture analysis remains valid over extended time periods. Furthermore, beyond reproducing the desired classical dynamics, this approach provides intriguing quantum corrections previously suggested by Dvali, Gomez, and Zell.

The universal approximation theorem posits that shallow neural networks can model any function. In these networks, inputs to neurons in each layer consist of a weighted sum of outputs from the preceding layer, followed by the application of an activation function. While such functions excel when outputs represent linear combinations of input data, neural networks often overfit when attempting to learn functions involving the product of inputs. This paper introduces a pair of activation functions based on logarithmic properties, designed to convert multiplicative operations into linear expressions for effective learning via backpropagation. Furthermore, we aim to generalize this methodology to more complex arithmetic functions and evaluate their accuracy on disjoint distributions relative to the training set.

This study explores the physics of photonic band structures arising in moiré patterns formed by overlapping two one-dimensional (1D) photonic crystal slabs with mismatched periods. The resulting band structure stems from the interaction between intra-layer and inter-layer coupling mechanisms, which can be adjusted by varying the separation distance between the layers. We develop an effective Hamiltonian that accurately captures the system's essential physics and replicates numerical simulations of electromagnetic solutions. Notably, we observe "magic distances" where photonic flatbands emerge across the entire Brillouin zone of the moiré superlattice. These flatband modes are shown to be strongly localized within a single moiré period. Furthermore, we propose a single-band tight-binding model describing the moiré minibands, where the tunneling rate can be continuously controlled via inter-layer strength. Our findings demonstrate that the band structure of bilayer photonic moiré systems can be engineered similarly to their electronic and excitonic counterparts, potentially enabling the investigation of many-body physics at photonic moiré flatbands and the development of novel optoelectronic devices.

Recent advancements in Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have sparked significant interest in Distributed Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithms. However, traditional Model-Based (MB) or Model-Free (MF) RL methods are ill-suited for MARL due to their reliance on fixed reward models for value function learning. Although DNN-based solutions excel in single-agent settings, they struggle to generalize effectively to the complexities of multi-agent scenarios. Specifically, current DNN approaches for multi-agent environments often suffer from overfitting, high sensitivity to parameter choices, and sample inefficiency. To address these limitations, this paper introduces the Multi-Agent Adaptive Kalman Temporal Difference (MAK-TD) framework and its Successor Representation-based variant, MAK-SR. The core objective is to leverage the distinct capabilities of Kalman Filtering (KF), particularly its ability to model uncertainty and perform online second-order learning. The proposed frameworks account for the continuous, high-dimensional action spaces inherent in multi-agent environments by utilizing Kalman Temporal Difference (KTD) to manage parameter uncertainty. Within this KTD framework, the Successor Representation learning process is formulated as a filtering problem, employing Radial Basis Function (RBF) estimators to map continuous spaces into feature vectors. Additionally, Multiple Model Adaptive Estimation (MMAE) is adopted to learn localized reward functions, overcoming the absence of prior knowledge regarding observation noise covariance and observation mappings. The efficacy of the MAK-TD/SR frameworks is validated through experiments conducted on OpenAI Gym MARL benchmarks.

This study revisits the problem of a thin superconducting film subjected to a parallel magnetic field, originally addressed by Ginzburg and Landau near the critical temperature, using microscopic BCS theory for arbitrary temperatures while incorporating pair-breaking and transport scattering effects. Although the results confirm experimental observations of $T_c$ enhancement due to the magnetic field, we demonstrate that transport scattering shifts the phase transition boundary to higher temperatures and fields across nearly all practical scattering rates. However, this enhancement vanishes in the dirty limit. Furthermore, we examine notable phenomena such as re-entrant superconductivity in the phase boundary induced by pair-breaking magnetic ions distributed on one film surface, features that currently await experimental confirmation.

This work addresses data gathering from a continent-wide network of energy-harvesting sensors designed for tracking mobile assets in rural settings. Due to application constraints, the proposed architecture features a highly asymmetric design where duty-cycled sensor nodes communicate with powered base stations. We investigate a new scheduling optimization problem for mobile sensor networks that harvest energy, aiming to maximize data collection within limits imposed by radio link quality and energy harvesting efficiency, while guaranteeing fair data reception. We demonstrate that this problem is NP-complete and introduce a heuristic algorithm capable of approximating the optimal schedule in polynomial time. Furthermore, the algorithm adapts to various energy harvesting scenarios, including progressive inputs like solar power and opportunistic, bursty inputs like Wireless Power Transfer. Using empirical data on link quality, solar energy, and WPT efficiency, we evaluate the algorithm through extensive simulations against state-of-the-art methods. Results indicate that our approach achieves high data reception rates across diverse fairness and node lifetime constraints.

We introduce HCFormer, a deep neural network architecture for image segmentation that utilizes hierarchical clustering. By framing semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation as pixel clustering tasks, our approach employs bottom-up hierarchical clustering. This method eliminates the need for a pixel decoder prior to the segmentation head, streamlining the pipeline and enhancing both accuracy and interoperability. Since pixel clustering serves as a unified strategy for diverse segmentation types, HCFormer can handle semantic, instance, and panoptic tasks within a single architecture. Experimental results demonstrate that HCFormer matches or outperforms baseline methods across all categories, achieving 55.5 mIoU on ADE20K for semantic segmentation, 47.1 AP on COCO for instance segmentation, and 55.7 PQ on COCO for panoptic segmentation.

Range-extended electric vehicles (REVs) merge the efficiency and eco-friendliness of battery-electric motors with the extended range of internal combustion engines. This hybrid approach is especially beneficial for time-sensitive delivery routes in crowded cities, where the time required to recharge all-electric vehicles makes them economically unviable. However, switching between electric and fossil fuel modes introduces higher costs, emissions, and reduced efficiency. This study investigates this heterogeneous vehicle routing problem using two methodologies: an exact branch-price-and-cut algorithm and an iterated tabu search metaheuristic. Methodologically, the exact algorithm provides robust lower bounds that validate the near-optimality of the metaheuristic results. From a policy perspective, a large-scale case study of parcel deliveries in the Chicago metropolitan area quantifies operational metrics such as energy expenses and vehicle miles traveled (VMT). The findings indicate that deploying approximately 20% of REVs with a modest 33-mile electric range can reduce energy costs by up to 17% while increasing VMT by less than 0.5%. Extending the electric range to 60 miles yields only a 4% further cost reduction, a benefit that could alternatively be achieved by reducing average service time by one minute or increasing driver working hours by one hour. Ultimately, this research identifies critical areas for improvement for vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and policymakers.

We introduce MC-CIM, a compute-in-memory (CIM) architecture designed to deliver robust, low-power Bayesian edge intelligence. Since deterministic deep neural networks (DNNs) lack the ability to represent prediction uncertainties, they pose significant risks in safety-critical domains like surgical robotics. To mitigate this, Bayesian inference has emerged as a solution, enabling the extraction of both predictions and confidence levels for risk-aware decision-making. However, exact Bayesian inference is computationally intensive and ill-suited for real-time edge deployment. As a more efficient alternative, Monte Carlo Dropout (MC-Dropout) offers high robustness with reduced complexity. To further enhance efficiency, we propose a novel CIM module capable of performing in-memory probabilistic dropout alongside in-memory weight-input scalar products. Additionally, we present a compute-reuse strategy for MC-Dropout, allowing successive iterations to leverage prior product-sum computations. We also detail an optimal ordering of random instances using combinatorial optimization to minimize the total MC-Dropout workload. The framework's effectiveness is demonstrated through MNIST character recognition and visual odometry for autonomous drones, where it reliably provides prediction confidence despite hardware non-idealities. Implemented with a 16x31 SRAM array, 0.85 V supply, and 16nm low-standby power (LSTP) technology, the proposed MC-CIM consumes 27.8 pJ for 30 MC-Dropout inference instances in its optimal configuration, achieving a 43% energy reduction compared to standard execution.

This paper introduces the Graph Inception Diffusion Networks (GIDN) model, which extends graph diffusion across various feature spaces and employs inception modules to mitigate the computational burden of intricate network architectures. Evaluated on Open Graph Benchmark (OGB) datasets, GIDN achieves an 11% performance improvement over AGDN on the ogbl-collab dataset.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) adapt convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for use with graph-structured data, raising the question of how much the inherent graph topology in GNNs actually boosts performance compared to CNNs that disregard such structure. To investigate this, we propose "edge entropy" as a metric to gauge the potential advantage GNNs hold over CNNs. Empirical results from node classification tasks on both synthetic and real-world datasets indicate that lower edge entropy correlates with greater anticipated performance gains for GNNs, whereas higher edge entropy suggests more modest improvements.

Terminology extraction, synonymous with term extraction, serves as a subfield of information extraction, aiming to automatically identify pertinent words or phrases within a specific corpus. This paper examines an unsupervised approach for automated domain term extraction, which incorporates chunking and preprocessing steps alongside ranking domain-specific terms based on relevance and cohesion functions, specifically for the ICON 2020 shared task 2: TermTraction.

This study presents and investigates fractional measure-theoretic elliptic operators defined on the torus alongside a novel stochastic process termed W-Brownian motion. We derive key regularity and spectral properties for these operators, specifically establishing precise upper and lower bounds for the growth rate of eigenvalues within their associated spectral problem. Furthermore, we demonstrate the relationship between the Cameron-Martin space linked to W-Brownian motion and the Sobolev spaces associated with the aforementioned elliptic operators. The work concludes by outlining applications of this theoretical framework to stochastic partial differential equations.

This paper presents an agent-based framework for representing games, offering a compact solution for multi-party games within game theory. Drawing inspiration from process theory and process algebra, we also develop an algorithm that accepts a game defined in process algebra and computes its Nash equilibrium with linear space complexity.

Logic Programming using Prolog has been extensively employed for knowledge persistence in numerous systems. Many Prolog implementations feature bidirectional interfaces with other programming languages, particularly Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) languages. However, current development lacks tools and frameworks that facilitate the creation of systems utilizing logic predicate persistence in an agile and straightforward manner. Specifically, there is a need for a modern object-oriented and logic persistence provider that enables in-memory object manipulation while maintaining the persistence aspect through Logic Programming predicates. This work introduces a declarative mapping alternative to support such a provider. The proposed solution establishes a correspondence between Logic Programming predicates and an Object-Oriented approach, where each element in one paradigm reciprocates with an element in the other. This Object-Oriented representation of Logic Programming predicates enhances the facility for manipulating the elements that constitute knowledge.

Recommender systems are a critical component of e-commerce platforms, typically generating suggestions by aggregating extensive user data. However, malicious actors may attempt to manipulate these systems by injecting corrupt data points to exploit them for financial profit. To address this, we introduce a semi-supervised algorithm designed to detect such malicious entries. Our method utilizes a segment of the dataset presumed to be unpolluted to model the distribution of authentic data. By adapting the Generative Adversarial Network architecture to incorporate contextual user activity information, our approach enables the model to effectively differentiate between legitimate data points and those that have been injected.

Inspired by recent studies on Delaunay triangulations of hyperbolic surfaces, this work investigates the minimum vertex count required for such triangulations. First, we demonstrate that every hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ admits a simplicial Delaunay triangulation with $O(g)$ vertices, where edges represent distance paths. Next, we construct a specific class of hyperbolic surfaces that prove this bound is optimal. Finally, we establish that the general $\Omega(\sqrt{g})$ lower bound for the number of vertices in a simplicial triangulation of a topological surface of genus $g$ is also tight when applied to hyperbolic surfaces.

We investigate moving Lifshitz branes within Einstein-Maxwell-Dilaton gravity featuring a generic dynamical critical exponent $z > 1$ and non-zero linear momentum along the boundary. This setup serves as a holographic dual for a non-equilibrium steady state in a quantum critical fluid that exhibits Lifshitz scale invariance but lacks boost symmetry. By applying an appropriate holographic renormalization technique, we derive the non-relativistic stress tensor complex for the dual field theory. Consequently, the resulting black brane hydrodynamics and thermodynamics offer a specific holographic realization of a Lifshitz perfect fluid characterized by a generic dynamical critical exponent.

The COVID-19 pandemic triggered an "infodemic," spreading misinformation regarding the virus and its treatments, which hinders the public's adoption of essential health measures. To address this, we introduce a novel multimodal dataset comprising labeled news articles and tweets about the COVID-19 vaccine, integrating images, text, and temporal data. The dataset includes 2,593 news articles from 80 publishers gathered between February 16, 2020, and May 8, 2021, alongside 24,184 Twitter posts collected from April 17, 2021, to May 8, 2021. To classify news credibility, we merged ratings from the Medias Bias Chart and Media Bias/Fact Check (MBFC) into two categories: reliable and unreliable, a dual-filter approach that enhances labeling precision. Additionally, we developed a stance detection method to categorize tweets into three credibility levels: reliable, unreliable, and inconclusive. The paper presents various statistics and analytics, including publisher distribution, publication timelines, and topic analysis. We also propose a new architecture designed to distinguish between misinformation and truth in news data, establishing a baseline with an F-Score of 0.919 and an accuracy of 0.882 for fake news detection. Furthermore, benchmark results for misinformation detection on the tweet dataset are provided. This multimodal resource is intended to support research on the COVID-19 vaccine, specifically in areas such as misinformation detection and analyzing the impact of false vaccine-related information.

The impact of dispersal on the stability and synchrony of metacommunities is a significant area of interest in theoretical ecology. Dispersal is recognized for fostering both synchrony, which raises extinction risks, and spatial heterogeneity, which supports population persistence. While various studies have explored different dispersal variants in spatially distributed ecological communities, the effects of controlled dispersal on metacommunity stability and persistence remain unclear, especially given that environmental changes strongly influence dispersal patterns. This study examines the consequences of restricting immigration within a two-patch prey-predator metacommunity across both local and spatial scales. We observe that limiting predator dispersal causes a monotonic reduction in the spread of inhomogeneous stable steady states (asynchronous states). Conversely, at the local scale, the spread of these inhomogeneous steady states initially rises to a critical threshold of the limiting factor, enhancing metacommunity persistence, before declining further as the limiting factor decreases, depending on local interactions. Notably, restricting prey dispersal promotes inhomogeneous steady states across a broad parameter region, thereby boosting persistence at both spatial and local scales. Additionally, we demonstrate similar qualitative dynamics in a wide class of complex networks comprising numerous patches. We also derive various bifurcation curves and stability conditions for inhomogeneous steady states, which align closely with simulation results. Consequently, our insights into the effects of limited dispersal can aid in developing conservation strategies for ecological communities.

Indium Arsenide (InAs) quantum wells (QWs) situated near their surfaces hold significant promise for creating semiconductor-superconductor heterostructures, primarily because they facilitate robust hybridization between the two-dimensional states within the well and those in the superconductor. This study reports on InAs QWs operating in the quantum Hall regime when brought into proximity with superconducting NbTiN. Our observations reveal a negative downstream resistance accompanied by a decrease in Hall (upstream) resistance, findings that align with exceptionally high Andreev conversion efficiency. We interpret the experimental results using a generalized Landauer-Büttiker formalism that incorporates Andreev reflection processes. We attribute the superior efficiency of Andreev conversion in these devices to the high transparency of the InAs/NbTiN interface, which enables strong hybridization between the quantum Hall edge modes and the superconductor's states.

We have introduced a framework of entanglement thermodynamics laws applicable to $T\bar{T}$-deformed conformal field theories (CFTs) and, more broadly, to $T^2$-deformed field theories. Specifically, the first law indicates that despite the non-trivial nature of the deformed theory, variations in entanglement entropy correspond directly to changes in the bending energy of the entangling surface, which we identify as decomposition energy. By examining the full spectrum of the deformed theory, we derive a second law that establishes an inequality originating from the saturation limit of the first law; this second law ensures the maintenance of the unitarity bound. The thermodynamic formulation of these principles necessitates defining the temperature of deformation and characterizing its properties, a focus of our third law. This analysis employs a holographic approach, with each result extended to higher dimensions.

We establish that the slice rank (a combinatorial concept by Tao related to the cap-set problem), analytic rank (a Fourier-theoretic concept by Gowers and Wolf), and geometric rank (an algebro-geometric concept by Kopparty, Moshkovitz, and Zuiddam) coincide for 3-tensors up to an absolute constant. Consequently, we derive significant trade-offs regarding the arithmetic complexity of biased bilinear maps and distinguish between exact and average-case computation of such maps. This finding resolves open questions posed by Haramaty and Shpilka [STOC 2010] and Lovett [Discrete Anal. 2019] specifically for 3-tensors.

Point cloud registration serves as a critical stage in numerous processing workflows, yet the majority of existing algorithms are evaluated on privately collected, non-shared data. These isolated datasets typically address only narrow use cases, hindering the generalization of results. While several public datasets have been introduced, individually they encompass only specific environments and predominantly data from a single sensor type. To address these limitations, we have developed a comprehensive benchmark for localization and mapping tasks that aggregates multiple publicly available sources. This approach ensures coverage across diverse environments and sensor types. Additionally, we have rigorously verified the ground truth quality; for datasets where original authors failed to report measuring system accuracy, we estimated it using a novel method based on iterative registration. Accompanying the data is a wide array of registration scenarios designed to represent various initial misalignments, overlap levels, and problem types. Finally, we introduce a performance metric that synthesizes rotation and translation errors to facilitate objective algorithm comparisons. Our goal is to motivate researchers to adopt shared public benchmarks rather than ad-hoc data collection, thereby ensuring the objectivity and repeatability essential to scientific inquiry.

This study examines how a terahertz field impacts the breathing dynamics of double-stranded DNA. By modeling the spontaneous creation of spatially localized openings in a damped and driven DNA chain, we observe that linear instabilities cause dynamic dimerization, whereas genuine local strand separations depend on a threshold amplitude mechanism. Based on these findings, we propose that specific terahertz radiation exposure could substantially alter the natural dynamics of DNA, potentially influencing complex molecular processes such as gene expression and DNA replication.

The non-Hermitian, parity-time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric Anderson model features an exceptional point (EP) at a coupling $g=1$ that stays unrenormalized despite interactions (Lourenco et al, arXiv:1806.03116), coinciding with the quantum critical point (QCP) for Kondo destruction. In this study, we examine a quantum dot coupled to metallic leads with Rashba spin-orbit coupling ($\lambda$). We demonstrate that non-Hermitian hybridization allows $\lambda$ to renormalize the EP even without interactions, thereby extending $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry stability beyond $g=1$. Using exact diagonalization on a zero-bandwidth, three-site model, we find that the QCP and EP separate, with the Kondo destruction critical point fixed at $g_c=1$ while the exceptional coupling satisfies $g_{\scriptscriptstyle{EP}} > 1$ for all $U\neq 0$ and $\lambda\geq 0$ (excluding $\lambda=U/2$). At the specific line $\lambda=U/2$, the critical point and EP merge again at $g_c=g_{\scriptscriptstyle{EP}}=1$. Furthermore, applying the slave-boson approach to the finite-bandwidth model reveals that in the strong coupling regime, both $\lambda$ and interactions collaborate to significantly lower the Kondo destruction critical point below the value observed when $\lambda=0$.

Verified controller synthesis relies on world models that encompass all possible behaviors of humans, robots, auxiliary equipment, and the controller itself. These models facilitate quantitative risk assessment, often through stochastic model checking, by defining a spectrum of controller behaviors where some—when executed correctly—ensure acceptable real-world risk levels, contingent on conservative stochastic assumptions. Consequently, the synthesis process identifies a controller behavior with an acceptable risk profile. Nevertheless, due to discrepancies arising from abstraction, formalism, and tool boundaries, rigorous testing remains essential alongside verified synthesis for robotic and autonomous systems. Generally, safety-critical system standards mandate testing as a prerequisite for certification and service entry. This paper outlines a methodology for comprehensively testing synthesised supervisory controllers designed to enforce safety in domains like human-robot collaboration and autonomous driving. While controller code is derived from the selected behavior, formally and comprehensively verifying the code generator is often impractical. Instead, an abstract test reference—a symbolic finite state machine with simpler semantics—is generated. From this reference, a complete test suite is constructed to demonstrate observational equivalence between the abstract model and the concrete controller code executing on the control system platform.

Although individuals with a passion for painting often face significant challenges due to visual impairments, their desire to create art, akin to that of Leonardo da Vinci, remains strong. To bridge this gap, we propose a painting navigation system designed to assist blind users in artistic creation. This system integrates a cognitive component with a guidance module, utilizing QR codes for drawing board positioning, target detection for brush navigation, and real-time brush tracking. It employs voice-based human-computer interaction alongside a streamlined coding rule for position data. Additionally, a specific criterion has been established to efficiently determine brush-target alignment. Experimental outcomes indicate that thermal curves derived from testers' faces reveal high acceptance rates among both blindfolded and blind participants. With a 1-second prompt frequency, the system achieved an 89% completion rate (SD: 8.37%) and a 347% overflow rate (SD: 162.14%). Furthermore, 74% of brush tip trajectories were classified as excellent or good, with a relative movement distance of 4.21 (SD: 2.51). These results demonstrate the feasibility of allowing blind individuals to experience the world through their hands. Future plans include deploying the "Angle's Eyes" application on mobile phones to enhance portability. A demonstration video of the system is accessible at: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.9760004.v1.

Lately, the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) and Krylov complexity have gained significant attention as metrics for quantifying operator growth. While OTOC is established to display exponential growth in chaotic systems—a finding supported by numerous prior studies—certain non-chaotic systems also exhibit chaotic-like OTOC behavior, failing to differentiate between saddle-dominated scrambling and true chaos. Similarly, under the universal operator growth hypothesis, Lanczos coefficients were expected to grow linearly in chaotic systems, representing the fastest possible rate. However, recent observations indicate that both Lanczos coefficients and K-complexity display chaotic behavior within the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) model, also rendering them unable to distinguish saddle-dominated scrambling from chaos. In this study, we calculate the Lanczos coefficients and K-complexity for an inverted harmonic oscillator and discover they likewise exhibit chaotic behavior, consistent with the LMG model results. Furthermore, by examining bounds on the quantum Lyapunov coefficient and the growth rate of Lanczos coefficients, we identify distinctions from chaotic systems. Finally, we analyze microcanonical K-complexity and compare its behavior with that of the OTOC.

This work examines the asymptotic behavior of the reaction-diffusion equation $\partial_t u=\Delta u +f(u)$ in $N$ spatial dimensions, specifically when the nonlinearity is bistable and the initial data has compact support. We establish the existence of a Lipschitz function $s^\infty$ defined on the unit sphere, ensuring that $u(t,x)$ converges uniformly over $\mathbb{R}^N$ as $t \to \infty$ to the profile $U_{c_*}\bigg(|x|-c_*t + \frac{N-1}{c_*} \mathrm{ln}t + s^\infty\Big(\frac{x}{|x|}\Big)\bigg)$, where $U_{c*}$ represents the unique one-dimensional traveling wave. These findings extend previous research, which either located solution level sets with $o_{t\to+\infty}(t)$ accuracy or precisely determined them for nearly radial initial conditions.

Large language models, typically trained over hundreds of thousands of compute days, exhibit impressive zero- and few-shot learning abilities. However, their high computational demands make replication costly, and those accessible via APIs do not allow access to full model weights, hindering research. We introduce Open Pre-trained Transformers (OPT), a collection of decoder-only pre-trained transformers spanning 125M to 175B parameters, designed for complete and responsible sharing with researchers. Our results demonstrate that OPT-175B matches the performance of GPT-3 while generating only one-seventh of the associated carbon emissions. Additionally, we are providing a logbook outlining the infrastructure hurdles encountered, alongside code to facilitate experimentation with all released models.

Previous research by \cite{Guo2019} established that both the Camassa-Holm and Novikov equations are ill-posed in $B_{p,r}^{1+1/p}(\mathbb{R})$ for $(p,r)\in[1,\infty]\times(1,\infty]$, whereas \cite{Ye} demonstrated well-posedness in $B_{p,1}^{1+1/p}(\mathbb{R})$ when $p\in[1,\infty)$. Furthermore, \cite{Guo} recently confirmed the ill-posedness of the Camassa-Holm equation in $B^{1}_{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R})$. This paper addresses the remaining open endpoint case, $r=1$, for the Novikov equation. Specifically, we demonstrate the ill-posedness of the Novikov equation in $B^{1}_{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R})$ through the phenomenon of norm inflation.
